title: FLNA-related periventricular nodular heterotopia with multisystem involvement: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background FLNA-related periventricular nodular heterotopia (PVNH) is an X-linked neuronal migration disorder classically associated with epilepsy. Accumulating evidence indicates that it is a multisystem disorder involving cardiac valvular, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic manifestations. We report a patient with an unusually comprehensive multisystem phenotype to emphasize the need for systematic extracranial evaluation in FLNA-related PVNH. Case presentation: A 33-year-old woman presented with two decades of headache and palpitations. Physical examination revealed digital clubbing and prominently dilated cardiac valves. Brain MRI demonstrated bilateral periventricular heterotopia. Enhanced whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic nonsense variant in FLNA (NM_001110556.2:c.2193C > G, p.Tyr731Ter). Multisystem involvement comprised focal epilepsy, polyvalvular regurgitation, interstitial lung disease, and ophthalmologic abnormalities. Seizures were controlled with oxcarbazepine and lamotrigine, and the patient was referred for coordinated cardiologic, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic follow-up. Conclusions FLNA-related PVNH should be managed as a multisystem disorder rather than isolated epilepsy. Routine cardiovascular, pulmonary, and ophthalmologic screening, combined with genetic counseling for X-linked dominant transmission, should be integrated into standard care.

title: Spatial Alignment of Parkinson’s Disease-Related Quantitative MRI Alterations with Dopaminergic Topography
abstract: Abstract Objective Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by a degeneration of dopaminergic neurons not only in the nigrostriatal pathways, but also in subcortical and cortical structures. Given the widespread dopaminergic innervation, PD dopamine-related dysfunction may contribute to microstructural alterations beyond the primary site of pathology. Multiparametric mapping (MPM) enables quantification of tissue biophysical properties informing the brain’s microstructure. We hypothesized that PD-related MPM alterations would show distinct spatial associations with pre- and postsynaptic dopaminergic markers. Methods 31 patients with PD and 68 healthy controls underwent a 3T MRI. We used unthresholded MPM t-maps derived from group-difference analysis to assess spatial correlation with PET-derived maps of the dopamine transporter (DAT), [ 18 F]-fluoro-L-DOPA (FDOPA), and dopamine D1 and D2 receptors. Results Proton density alterations negatively correlated with DAT (rho = 0.355, p spatial = 0.0010) and FDOPA (rho = 0.168, p FDR = 0.0080) across whole-brain gray matter. Subcortically, MPM-dopaminergic associations were structure-specific, showing concordant, same-direction associations between FDOPA and D1. Cortically, associations were more consistent, predominantly negative and driven by DAT and FDOPA. Within cortical ROIs, presupplementary and supplementary motor areas showed the most robust associations, driven by proton density (preSMA: rho = 0.428 to 0.760; SMA: rho = 0.284 to 0.789, all p FDR < 0.0001). Interpretation: PD-related microstructural-dopaminergic associations were structure- and modality-specific. Subcortically, FDOPA and D1 consistently tracked microstructural alterations, potentially reflecting coupled degeneration of dopaminergic synthesis capacity and postsynaptic receptor density. Cortically, DAT and FDOPA most robustly tracked proton density-related alterations, potentially indicating distinct and mainly neuroinflammation-driven microstructural processes beyond the primary nigrostriatal network.

title: Neuro-JEPA: Building and Evaluating Health-System Scale Neuroimaging Foundation Models with Mixture of Experts
abstract: Abstract Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain routinely combines complementary contrasts—including T1-weighted (T1w), T2-weighted (T2w) and FLAIR sequences—to capture anatomy and pathology. Although foundation models trained on large neuroimaging datasets have shown promise, it remains unclear whether they effectively integrate these complementary contrasts across diverse clinical settings. Here we present Neuro-JEPA, a multimodal foundation model that learns unified representations across structural brain MRIs. Neuro-JEPA combines latent predictive learning with a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture to encode multiple MRI contrasts within a single model. The model is pretrained on 1.55 million scans from 428,647 clinical imaging studies spanning T1w, T2w and FLAIR sequences. The model performance is evaluated on 47 downstream tasks across three independent health systems and 12 public datasets, encompassing single-contrast, multimodal and cross-domain applications. Across these evaluations, Neuro-JEPA achieved the strongest overall performance and generalized robustly across heterogeneous cohorts, outperforming existing neuroimaging foundation models and strong conventional baselines in the majority of comparisons despite using less than one-third of the pretraining data of leading models. Performance gains were particularly pronounced in data-scarce settings, reaching up to 15% over prior foundation models for clinically important pathologies including gliosis and multiple sclerosis. Neuro-JEPA showed clinically relevant capabilities across domains, including prediction of amyloid status and progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer’s disease dementia, stroke identification and classification, and prediction of post-stroke functional outcome and length of stay. Together, these results show that data scale, curation and principled model design can act synergistically to produce broadly transferable neuroimaging representations, and establish Neuro-JEPA as a scalable framework toward general-purpose multimodal foundation models for neurological imaging.

title: PSA Trends and Clinical Outcomes Following Radiotherapy Combined with Androgen Deprivation Therapy for Prostate Cancer: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study from Saudi Arabia
abstract: Abstract Background Combined external-beam radiotherapy and androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is standard treatment for men with intermediate- to high-risk prostate cancer, but outcome data from the Gulf region remain limited despite a rising regional disease burden. We evaluated longitudinal PSA response, treatment-related morbidity, and oncological outcomes in patients treated with curative-intent radiotherapy plus ADT, characterising PSA kinetics over the first nine months of treatment and identifying clinical predictors of the PSA trajectory. Methods In this retrospective cohort study at King Abdulaziz Medical City, Riyadh, we included all adult patients with prostate cancer who received radiotherapy combined with ADT and had complete treatment and follow-up records. Demographic, clinical, and treatment data were extracted from electronic medical records, with serial PSA recorded at baseline and at 3, 6, and 9 months. Changes in PSA from baseline were assessed with the paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and a linear mixed-effects model (random intercept per patient; fixed effects for time, age, Gleason group, and metastatic status; PSA log₁₀[PSA + 1]-transformed) was used to identify predictors of longitudinal PSA levels. Results Seventy-four patients were included (median age 68.0 years, IQR: 63.0–75.0; median PSA at diagnosis 17.3 ng/mL, IQR: 9.3–33.0), 64.9% with Gleason group 4–5 disease. Most received hypofractionated radiotherapy (median 60 Gy in 20 fractions) with a single ADT cycle (90.4%), predominantly leuprolide (91.8%). PSA fell progressively at every interval (all p < 0.001): median reductions of 91.9%, 99.2%, and 99.7% from baseline at 3, 6, and 9 months, with the proportion achieving a ≥ 50% reduction rising from 73.2% to 93.0% over the same period; median PSA nadir was 0.028 ng/mL (IQR: 0.024–0.560). On adjusted mixed-effects modelling, reductions at each time point remained significant independent of age and Gleason group (β = −0.81 to − 1.13 versus baseline, all p < 0.001), while metastatic disease at presentation predicted higher longitudinal PSA levels. Disease recurrence occurred in 5.4% of patients, with a median time to recurrence of 68.5 months; treatment-related toxicity was low, with urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction each affecting fewer than 7% of patients at 12 months. Conclusions In this predominantly high-risk, real-world cohort, combined radiotherapy and ADT produced rapid, deep, and durable PSA suppression with low toxicity and low biochemical recurrence, irrespective of baseline Gleason grade. These findings support the effectiveness and tolerability of this regimen outside the trial setting and provide PSA kinetic benchmarks from an underrepresented population that may complement randomised evidence, though prospective data incorporating PSMA-PET-based surveillance are needed to confirm whether early deep response translates into durable survival benefit.

title: A Pipeline for ADNI Resting-State Functional MRI Processing and Quality Control
abstract: Abstract The Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) provides a comprehensive multimodal neuroimaging resource for studying aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, its resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data remain underutilized, in part due to challenges with data processing driven by considerable variability in acquisition protocols, inconsistent organization, missing or incomplete imaging sessions, and frequency of data quality issues due to participant motion and aging-related factors. To facilitate widespread use of ADNI rs-fMRI data, we developed an open-source pipeline encompassing the download and organization of imaging and clinical data, conversion to Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), preprocessing with fMRIPrep, and automated quality control (QC). Our QC considers acquisition parameters and 16 structural and functional MRIQC image-quality metrics, flagging scans that fall outside acceptable ranges based on expert input and robust outlier detection techniques. Processed imaging sessions are matched to temporally aligned clinical assessments to produce an analysis-ready dataset. Applying the pipeline to more than 2,800 sessions from ADNI GO, ADNI 2, and ADNI 3 yielded 2,086 quality-checked functional and structural MRI sessions from 935 unique participants. Exclusions occurred at every processing stage and were driven primarily by BIDS conversion errors, image quality flags, and preprocessing- or motion-related failures. The open-source pipeline described in this work produces one of the largest pre-processed, quality controlled, and analysis-ready functional and structural MRI datasets yet available for studying aging and AD. It lowers barriers to large-cohort and longitudinal neuroimaging research and supports large-scale neuroimaging biomarker discovery in AD.

title: Thenar Muscle Thickness Assessed by Point-of-Care Ultrasound and Geriatric Vulnerability in Hospitalized Older Adults: A Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background Malnutrition and sarcopenia frequently coexist in hospitalized older adults. Thenar muscle thickness (TMT) may provide a pragmatic correlate of geriatric vulnerability, but its clinical relevance is unestablished. Methods This retrospective, single-centre, cross-sectional pilot study analyzed 50 hospitalized patients aged 75 years or older, admitted between October and December 2024. Unadjusted Spearman correlations assessed associations between TMT and Mini Nutritional Assessment–Short Form (MNA-SF), Braden, and Conley scores. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were calculated for these three correlations. Results Mean age was 86.2 years; 60.0% of participants were women. Mean TMT was 2.62 cm (SD, 0.48). Overall, 84.0% of patients were malnourished or at risk of malnutrition, 66.0% had high pressure-injury risk, and 90.0% had a Conley score indicating fall risk. Higher TMT correlated with higher MNA-SF (rho = 0.760; 95% CI, 0.595–0.859; P < 0.001) and Braden scores (rho = 0.560; 95% CI, 0.340–0.729; P < 0.001), and with lower Conley scores (Rho = − 0.406; 95% CI, − 0.627 to − 0.141; P = 0.003). Associations remained directionally consistent after adjustment for age and sex: partial rho was 0.753 (95% CI, 0.572–0.865) for MNA-SF, 0.510 (95% CI, 0.251–0.709) for Braden, and − 0.361 (95% CI, − 0.602 to − 0.054) for Conley. TMT was not significantly associated with length of stay (Rho = − 0.240; P = 0.093). Conclusions In very old hospitalized adults, lower TMT was associated with poorer nutritional status and greater fall and pressure-injury risk. TMT may complement multidimensional geriatric assessment, but the small, unadjusted pilot design and absence of a sarcopenia reference standard preclude diagnostic or independent prognostic claims.

title: Preoperative diffusion-perivascular MRI burden and postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation in Parkinson disease
abstract: Abstract Postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation may reflect pre-existing brain vulnerability, but the preoperative imaging correlates of this vulnerability remain uncertain. We examined whether a combined diffusion and perivascular imaging burden was associated with delirium after bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation. This single-centre observational cohort included 100 patients with Parkinson disease undergoing bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation and 32 healthy controls scanned with the same preoperative MRI protocol. Delirium was assessed during postoperative days using the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale with clinical adjudication. Age- and sex-adjusted reference models fitted in healthy controls were used to standardise tract diffusion metrics, diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space, and basal ganglia enlarged perivascular space counts. Directionally aligned diffusion and perivascular scores were averaged with equal domain weights. Patients who developed postoperative delirium (n = 30) had higher combined burden than those who did not (n = 70; 95% CI, 0.584 to 1.526; q<.001). Using Firth penalised logistic regression, higher combined burden remained associated with postoperative delirium after adjustment for age, sex, education, Mini-Mental State Examination score, disease duration, and motor severity (95% CI, 1.49 to 4.25; Wald P<.001). Higher burden was also associated with longer delirium duration and higher peak screening scores among affected patients. Exploratory internal prediction yielded an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.701 after adding burden to clinical variables, compared with 0.538 for clinical variables alone. These findings support preoperative diffusion-perivascular burden as a candidate marker of perioperative neuropsychiatric vulnerability requiring multicentre validation.

title: Transthoracic echocardiography for initial screening of single coronary artery anomaly: a case with multimodal imaging evaluation
abstract: Abstract Single coronary artery anomaly (SCA) is a rare congenital coronary malformation with only one aortic coronary ostium supplying the whole myocardium. Clinical outcomes mainly depend on the anatomical course of the aberrant vessel. We report a 73-year-old female presenting with intermittent precordial chest pain. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a dilated right coronary artery (RCA) with normal ostial location, non-visualization of the left coronary artery ostium, and diastolic low-resistance arterial flow signal within the interventricular septum along the expected left anterior descending artery (LAD) territory. Coronary computed-tomography angiography (CCTA) demonstrated right-dominant coronary circulation, absence of the native left coronary artery, and an abnormally extended posterior descending artery travelling into the anterior interventricular groove. Multimodal imaging highly suggested Lipton-Yamanaka type R-I SCA. The patient received conservative medical therapy for co-existing mild coronary atherosclerosis. This case underlines TTE as a valuable first-line screening tool for congenital coronary anomalies. Nevertheless, definitive subtyping requires CCTA or invasive coronary angiography.

title: Agreement of Radiographic Parameters Between Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs from Weight-Bearing Cone-Beam CT and Whole-Spine Radiographs
abstract: Abstract Purpose Current spinal deformity diagnosis relies on whole-spine radiographs, while Weight-bearing Radiology 3D (WR3D) offers accurate, low-dose three-dimensional reconstruction in the standing position. This study aims to evaluate the potential of digitally reconstructed radiographs (DRRs) generated from WR3D images as a substitute for standard whole-spine radiographs. Methods In this retrospective comparative study of 67 patients who underwent both WR3D examination and whole-spine radiographs, DRRs were generated using segmentation and projection algorithms. Two observers independently measured coronal and sagittal radiographic parameters of the spine and pelvis on both imaging modalities, with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) calculated. Paired samples t -tests and Bland-Altman analyses were performed, with mean absolute errors (MAEs) and Pearson correlation coefficients calculated. Results DRRs exhibited superior interobserver reliability compared to radiographs, particularly for pelvic incidence (PI, ICC = 0.95 vs. 0.70), pelvic tilt (PT, ICC = 0.98 vs. 0.83), sacral slope (SS, ICC = 0.94 vs. 0.79), and upper thoracic parameters. High agreement between the two imaging modalities was observed in measurements of all coronal parameters, cervical lordosis (C2-C7), thoracolumbar kyphosis (T10-L2), lumbar lordosis (L4-S1, L1-S1), PI, and PT ( p > 0.05), while differences were observed for other sagittal parameters ( p < 0.05). Conclusions DRR images based on WR3D show high agreement with radiographs for measuring most structural parameters. However, certain differences exist for global balance parameters and sagittal curvature parameters.

However, certain differences exist for global balance parameters and sagittal curvature parameters.

title: Evaluating the Osteogenic potential of S. officinale against Glucocorticoid-induced Osteoporosis using in vivo model
abstract: Abstract Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis is characterized by impaired bone formation, increased bone resorption and disruption of bone mineralization. The present study investigated the osteoprotective potential of Symphytum officinale ( S. officinale ) aqueous root extract using a dexamethasone-induced osteoporosis model in adult zebrafish ( Danio rerio ). Phytochemical screening and LC–MS analysis were performed to characterize the extract, followed by developmental toxicity assessment. Adult zebrafish were divided into control, dexamethasone-treated and low- and high-dose S. officinale -treated groups. Bone regeneration and mineralization were evaluated using histopathology, Alizarin Red staining, scale morphometry and ICP-MS analysis of calcium and phosphorus. Hydroxyproline, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) assays were performed to assess collagen content and bone remodelling. The extract showed the presence of alkaloids, terpenoids, phytosterols and other bioactive constituents, including quercetin derivatives and biochanin A, while no developmental toxicity was observed at the tested concentrations. Dexamethasone induced marked alterations in tissue architecture, reduced mineral deposition and scale size and disrupted calcium and phosphorus levels. S. officinale treatment improved skeletal morphology, mineralization, scale size and mineral content, with pronounced effects on several parameters at the higher dose. The extract also modulated hydroxyproline, ALP and TRAP activities, indicating concentration-dependent effects on bone remodelling. Hence, S. officinale demonstrates osteoprotective potential against dexamethasone-induced skeletal alterations in zebrafish.

title: Multi-Time-Point Kidney Segmentation in Lutetium-177 SPECT/CT Imaging Using a 3D Deep Learning Approach for Patient-Specific Dosimetry
abstract: Abstract Background : Multi-time-point kidney segmentation from Lutetium-177 (Lu-177) SPECT/CT is essential for patient-specific dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT). However, expert segmentation remains time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability, limiting its routine clinical use. Methods : This study compared the performance of four 3D deep-learning models including U-Net, Attention U-Net, UNETR, and SwinUNETR, for automated kidney segmentation and assessed their impact on internal dosimetry. A retrospective study was conducted using SPECT/CT datasets from patients who received Lu-177 PSMA or Lu-177 DOTATATE therapy. Performance was assessed using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and 95th percentile Hausdorff Distance (HD95). The best-performing model was applied to internal dosimetry calculations using MIRDcalc software. Results : SwinUNETR achieved the highest segmentation performance with DSC of 0.91±0.07 and HD95 of 12.50±14.82 mm. Dosimetry based on automated segmentation showed a mean absorbed dose difference of 10.28% relative to expert-based dosimetry. The DOTATATE group received mean kidney dose of 4.74±1.70 Gy/cycle, while the PSMA group received 1.73±1.89 Gy/cycle. Automated segmentation reduced processing time by 81-83% while maintaining accuracy comparable to expert segmentation. Conclusion : 3D deep-learning model, particularly SwinUNETR, demonstrates clinical feasibility for automated segmentation in Lu-177 SPECT/CT dosimetry workflows. Moreover, it significantly reduces clinician workload while maintaining clinically acceptable dosimetric accuracy.

title: Feasibility and Safety of Sheath-Assisted Limited Repair for Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Pseudoaneurysm
abstract: Abstract Objective:To evaluate the technical feasibility, perioperative safety, and mid-term clinical outcomes of Sheath-Assisted Limited Repair (SALR) in anatomically suitable patients with iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms (FAP). Methods: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on 10 consecutive patients with iatrogenic FAP who met strict anatomical eligibility criteria and underwent SALR at Binzhou Medical University Hospital between January 2015 and June 2025. Anatomical eligibility was defined as a localized, puncture-related lesion where the arterial defect could be temporarily sealed with an appropriately sized sheath, without involvement of the femoral bifurcation. The primary endpoints were technical success rate, conversion to standard open repair (SOR), reoperation/reintervention, pseudoaneurysm recurrence, and wound-related complications (infection, lymphorrhea). Secondary endpoints included operative time, intraoperative blood loss, bed rest duration, length of stay, and 24-hour postoperative VAS pain scores. Data from 30 patients undergoing SOR were documented for comparative clinical benchmarking. Results: The primary endpoints demonstrated remarkable success in the SALR cohort: the technical success rate was 100% (10/10), with no intraoperative conversions to SOR (0%), zero reinterventions or reoperations, and no recurrence of pseudoaneurysm during a mean follow-up of 24 months. No wound infections or lymphatic leaks occurred (0%). Regarding secondary endpoints, the operative time was 40.5 ± 12.5 min, median intraoperative blood loss was 20 (10, 40) mL, postoperative bed rest was 8.5 ± 2.5 h, and median hospital stay was 3.0 (2.0, 4.0) days. The 24-hour postoperative VAS score was 1.58 ± 0.9. Postoperative ultrasound confirmed 100% patency of the treated arterial segment without stenosis. Conclusion: SALR is a safe, highly feasible, and minimally invasive technique for anatomically suitable iatrogenic FAP. By utilizing the vascular sheath for in situ temporary hemostasis, it completely eliminates the need for extensive vascular dissection and proximal/distal clamping, thereby achieving high technical success, preventing lymphorrhea, and markedly accelerating postoperative recovery.

title: Deep Learning-Based Sex Classification and Chronological Age-Group Estimation from Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Task Framework with Rank-Fusion and Tri-Loss Learning
abstract: Abstract The sex classification and chronological age-group estimation from the knee radiographs are a significant area of interest in forensic anthropology and clinical diagnostics. As the knee exhibits clear sexual dimorphism and predictable age-related morphological changes, knee radiographs provide a useful basis for demographic profiling. While most existing research focuses on pediatric maturation, relatively limited research has addressed automated, fine-grained frameworks for adult demographic assessment. This study proposes an automated, deep learning-based multi-task framework designed to extract demographic information from knee radiographs. The research is structured into two investigative tasks: Task 1 addresses sex classification through a Rank-Fusion Ensemble strategy, which combines the ranked predictions of multiple deep neural networks to identify sex-related morphological patterns. Task 2 focuses on chronological age-group estimation using a ConvNeXt-Tiny model. To capture the ordinal progression of chronological age groups, Task 2 utilizes a proposed Tri-Loss strategy that combines CORAL, Cross-Entropy, and Ordinal Regression loss functions. The results demonstrate promising performance for demographic estimation from knee radiographs. For sex classification, the Rank-Fusion Ensemble achieved an accuracy of 96.65% with an ROC-AUC of 0.9840. For chronological age-group estimation, the model reached a Top-1 accuracy of 71.29%. A detailed evaluation showed an ordinal MAE of 0.32 age-group intervals, suggesting that age-group predictions are largely aligned with adjacent categories, reflecting the ordinal and overlapping nature of age-related morphological variation in the knee. By utilizing knee radiographs as the primary imaging modality, the multi-task approach offers a quantitative alternative to traditional qualitative radiological observations in forensic and medical contexts.

title: Probable neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease in an Asian woman without detectable NOTCH2NLC repeat expansion on routine testing
abstract: Abstract Background: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) is a clinically heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder characterized by eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions. GGC repeat expansion in NOTCH2NLC is strongly associated with adult-onset NIID in East Asian populations. Fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS), associated with an FMR1 CGG premutation, can overlap with NIID clinically, radiologically, and pathologically. Negative targeted repeat-expansion results therefore require interpretation alongside clinicopathological findings. Case presentation: A 67-year-old Asian woman with no known family history of neurological disease developed progressive cognitive decline in 2021, followed by limb ataxia and bilateral lower-limb weakness. In 2025, her ADL and mRS scores were 51/56 and 3; MoCA and MMSE scores were 8/30 and 19/30. Electrophysiological findings suggested predominantly motor demyelinating polyneuropathy. Brain MRI showed bilateral corticomedullary-junction hyperintensities on DWI and confluent periventricular and deep white-matter abnormalities on FLAIR and T2WI. A skin biopsy obtained above the lateral malleolus showed eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions in sweat gland epithelial cells and fibroblasts, with positive SQSTM1/p62 and SUMO1 immunostaining. RP-PCR did not detect a NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansion. Both FMR1 alleles were reported to contain 29 CGG repeats, below the premutation range. During 14 months of follow-up, no impaired consciousness, seizures, or encephalopathy-like episodes occurred, and the mRS Scale score remained 3. Cognitive scores changed in opposite directions, precluding conclusions about cognitive change or treatment response. The clinical, radiological, and previously reported pathological findings supported probable NIID, apparently sporadic, without molecular confirmation. Conclusions: Characteristic MRI and skin biopsy findings remain diagnostically informative when routine NOTCH2NLC screening detects no expansion. FMR1 analysis aids differentiation from FXTAS. A negative targeted result alone should neither exclude NIID nor imply a novel causative gene; confirmation using an independent repeat-expansion assay or long-read sequencing should be considered when available.

title: Lightweight Pure 3D Lung Nodule Detection and Segmentation Network with Asymmetric Feature Interaction
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D CNNs) for lung nodule analysis face a tension between accuracy and computational cost: isotropic cubic kernels match anisotropic CT data poorly, detection and segmentation are modeled in isolation, and parameter-constrained networks collapse to the trivial all-background solution under class imbalance. This study proposes Light3D-NoduleNet, a lightweight pure 3D joint detection and segmentation network for edge deployment. An asymmetric 3D depthwise separable convolution factorizes the cubic kernel into in-plane and inter-slice branches, cutting kernel parameters by about 56%; a scale-aware efficient channel attention adapts its kernel size to the channel count; and a bidirectional feature interaction module exchanges a spatial attention map and a channel attention vector between the two branches, closing the loop between tasks. Joint training on LUNA16 and LIDC-IDRI uses dynamic loss masking. On LIDC-IDRI, the model reaches a Dice coefficient of 0.5233 (median 95% Hausdorff distance 6.00 mm) with 5.24 M parameters and 178.3 G FLOPs, exceeding reproduced 3D U-Net and V-Net by 0.1545 and 0.0701. Three variants lacking bidirectional interaction all stagnate at 0.2302 after 100 epochs, whereas the full model converges to 0.5233. On a 15 W Jetson Orin NX it runs at 3.0 FPS with 435 MB VRAM, indicating that bidirectional feature interaction is a necessary architectural condition for lightweight 3D networks to escape the trivial solution under extreme foreground-background imbalance.

title: When tiny lungs Struggle to breathe; a rare cause of Refractory Primary Pulmonary Hypertension
abstract: Abstract Alveolar capillary dysplasia with malpositioned pulmonary veins (ACD/MPV) is a lethal congenital lung disorder with a mortality rate of almost 100%. Infants deteriorate within the first 24 hours of life. Here, we present a 2-day old female child born of full term normal vaginal delivery and cried immediately after birth. The baby presented with Respiratory distress within 6 hours of life and was put on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. 2-D echo revealed no congenital heart disease. The child continued to have pulmonary hypertension non-responsive to pharmacotherapy and eventually passed away. A post mortem histopathology examination revealed immature lung parenchyma with arrest in the saccular phase, thickened alveolar septae with abnormally positioned pulmonary capillaries. Focally, there were thin-walled vessels invested in the same adventitial sheath as the pulmonary arteries. The pulmonary arterioles exhibited features of pulmonary artery hypertension. Based on this constellation of features, the baby was diagnosed with ACD/MPV. The rarity and the focal nature of this condition make it a diagnostic challenge in terms of awareness of this entity and subsequent interpretation. Conclusion : This case reiterates the importance of knowing and understanding normal histology. A high degree of clinical suspicion as well as expertise in the field of thoracic pathology is required for appropriate diagnosis.

title: Association of CPAK Phenotypes With Valgus Overcorrection After Robotic-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty
abstract: Abstract Objective To investigate the discrepancy between intraoperative coronal alignment (hip-knee-ankle angle, HKA) measured during MAKO robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (raTKA) and postoperative full-leg radiographs (FLR), analyze the influence of CPAK phenotypes (especially types II and V) on this alignment shift, and identify risk factors for valgus overcorrection. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 264 knees with knee osteoarthritis that underwent primary raTKA using the MAKO RIO system (Stryker, Kalamazoo, MI, USA) at a single center from August 2023 to December 2025. All patients had preoperative CT (for MAKO planning), complete intraoperative navigation logs, and standard weight-bearing FLR at 3 months postoperatively. Preoperative CT three-dimensional reconstruction was used to measure the mechanical medial proximal tibial angle (mMPTA) and mechanical lateral distal femoral angle (mLDFA), from which joint line obliquity (JLO) and arithmetic HKA (aHKA) were derived for CPAK classification. The primary outcome was ΔHKA = intraoperative HKA − postoperative HKA (varus as positive; thus ΔHKA > 0 indicated more valgus postoperatively). |ΔHKA| > 2° was defined as clinically significant alignment drift, and valgus overcorrection was defined as postoperative weight-bearing FLR HKA < − 2° in knees with (1) preoperative varus deformity (FLR HKA > 0° or CT aHKA < − 2°) and (2) a varus-alignment surgical plan (MAKO planned intraoperative HKA > 0°). Multivariable logistic regression assessed factors independently associated with valgus overcorrection, and multivariable linear regression assessed factors associated with continuous ΔHKA. Results Among 264 knees, CPAK type II accounted for 17.8% (47/264), type V for 7.6% (20/264), totaling 25.4% (67/264). Mean intraoperative MAKO varus was 2.30° ± 1.73°, while postoperative FLR showed varus of 1.37° ± 2.01°, with a mean ΔHKA of 0.93° ± 2.23°, indicating that postoperative weight-bearing alignment was systematically more valgus than intraoperative measurements (P < 0.001). Bland-Altman analysis using postoperative minus intraoperative HKA showed a mean difference of − 0.93° and 95% limits of agreement of − 5.30° to + 3.43°. Overall incidence of |ΔHKA| > 2° was 36.4% (96/264); 42.6% in type II and 45.0% in type V. Valgus overcorrection occurred in 28.4% (75/264) overall; the pre-specified merged II/V group had a rate of 35.8% (24/67) versus 25.9% (51/197) in non-II/V (Fisher's exact test, unadjusted P = 0.161). After adjusting for bone defect, mMPTA difference, MCL release, sex, and BMI, the II/V phenotype was independently associated with valgus overcorrection (OR = 2.68, 95% CI 1.27–5.63, P = 0.010). Conclusion The residual varus alignment measured intraoperatively by the MAKO system in the supine, non-weight-bearing, anesthetized state does not fully represent postoperative weight-bearing mechanical alignment; this difference is multifactorial. CPAK types II and V were associated with greater postoperative valgus drift and higher adjusted odds of valgus overcorrection. Intraoperative non-weight-bearing alignment measurements may not fully represent postoperative weight-bearing alignment. CPAK classification may be useful for individualized alignment planning in raTKA, although optimal phenotype-specific alignment targets require prospective validation.

title: [18F]NaF PET Radiomics and Coronary Calcium Score Progression: Associations Beyond Baseline Calcium Score and TBR
abstract: Abstract Background: [ 18 F]NaF positron emission tomography (PET) can quantify coronary calcification activity before coronary calcium score (CCS) progression, which is a surrogate measure of cardiovascular disease risk. It remains uncertain whether advanced PET quantification, including radiomics, improves prediction of CCS progression. Participants with type 2 diabetes underwent baseline [ 18 F]NaF PET/CT, baseline CCS and a follow-up CCS after 2 years. CCS progression was evaluated on a per-patient and a per-artery level. [ 18 F]NaF activity was evaluated using the TBR max , and radiomics features. Logistic regression models were used to determine the features most associated with CCS progression. Results: In total, 91 participants (median age [interquartile range]: 66 [60 – 70], 71.4% male) were examined. In total, 68 patients (74.7%) demonstrated CCS progression. Clinical variables and baseline CCS discriminated CCS progressors and non-progressors modestly (AUC 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.86). The TBR max demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.73–0.92), while multi-feature radiomics models achieved the highest discrimination performance (AUC 0.90, 95% CI 0.80–0.97). title: ROI-Guided Lesion Segmentation for Maize Disease Phenotyping in Field Images
abstract: Abstract Accurate delineation of disease lesions in field images can support objective crop-health monitoring and image-based phenotyping of maize foliar diseases. However, variable illumination, cluttered backgrounds, and irregular lesion morphology can reduce the reliability of lesion segmentation in field conditions. This study evaluates whether the spatial quality of detector-generated regions of interest (ROIs) influences downstream lesion segmentation when the segmentation network is held constant. A two-stage framework was developed in which DT-YOLO localizes symptomatic regions before lesion delineation by a standard DeepLabV3 + network. DT-YOLO was derived from YOLOv11n by integrating C3k2_DualPConv blocks, post-neck Triplet Attention, and Minimum Point Distance Intersection over Union (MPDIoU) loss. The dataset included 4,126 original maize leaf images representing healthy leaves, gray leaf spot, northern leaf blight, common rust, and maize streak virus; augmentation expanded the detection dataset to 7,427 images. Pixel-level lesion masks were manually prepared for 600 images, and an independent set of 100 images was used for end-to-end evaluation. DT-YOLO achieved 89.0% mAP@0.5 with 2.52 M parameters and 6.40 GFLOPs. Although its mAP@0.5:0.95, precision, and recall were lower than those of YOLOv11n, DT-YOLO increased the ROI Alignment Score from 0.382 to 0.635. When coupled with the unchanged DeepLabV3 + model, it achieved 63.20% mIoU and 65.95% Dice, compared with 62.96% mIoU and 64.98% Dice for the YOLOv11n-based cascade. The modest downstream improvement indicates that ROI spatial alignment can affect lesion delineation, while also showing that localization errors remain a major limitation of end-to-end performance. This modular framework provides an approach for maize disease phenotyping and field-image analysis in which localization and lesion segmentation can be independently evaluated and improved.

title: Outcomes of Repeat Stereotactic Radiosurgery for Locally Recurrent Brain Metastases Following Initial Stereotactic Radiosurgery
abstract: Abstract Background Local recurrence after stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS1) for brain metastases remains a therapeutic challenge, and optimal re-irradiation parameters are not well defined. This study evaluated local control (LC) and predictors of radiation necrosis (RN) following repeat stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS2) for previously irradiated brain metastases. Methods This retrospective study included patients treated with SRS2 for locally recurrent brain metastases after prior SRS1. Patients who had received whole-brain radiotherapy were excluded. Follow-up MRI scans were reviewed for LC and RN according to RANO criteria. Kaplan–Meier analysis was used for LC and RN-free survival. Cox regression analysis identified predictive factors. ROC curve analysis determined optimal dosimetric cut-off values. Results Forty patients with 59 locally recurrent brain metastases treated with SRS2 to the same lesion were analyzed. Median follow-up was 11 months (range, 2–83). Median SRS2 prescription dose was 24 Gy (range, 14–35) delivered in a median of 3 fractions (range, 1–5), and median GTV diameter was 2.1 cm (range, 0.3–7.6). One-year local progression-free survival was 57.5% while one-year RN-free survival was 80%. Higher SRS2 EQD 2 (10) (> 33.6 Gy; 63.8% vs 93.1%, p = 0.007), cumulative EQD 2 (10) (> 75 Gy; 63.2% vs 91.4%, p = 0.006), SRS2 BED 10 (> 83.7 Gy; 65.8% vs 90.9%, p = 0.013), and cumulative BED 10 (> 177 Gy; 65.2% vs 91.0%, p = 0.013) were associated with significantly increased RN risk without corresponding LC benefit. Age, sex, histology, location, prior surgery, GTV and PTV diameter and volume, SRS1–SRS2 interval, dosimetric indices, and systemic therapy were not significantly associated with LC or RN. Conclusions Repeat SRS is an effective and well-tolerated salvage treatment for locally recurrent brain metastases. Doses below the identified BED and EQD 2 thresholds were associated with a lower risk of RN without significantly compromising local control. Prospective studies are warranted to validate optimal re-SRS dose constraints and treatment strategies for recurrent brain metastases.

title: Diagnosis and treatment of isolated tuberculosis of the posterior spinal elements: A retrospective study of 15 cases
abstract: Abstract Background Isolated tuberculosis (TB) of the posterior spinal elements is rare and often difficult to diagnose. We present the clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, and long-term outcomes of 15 patients with isolated posterior element TB. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 15 consecutive patients treated between October 2013 and January 2021. The patients’ baseline clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings were analyzed. The following outcomes were assessed: erythrocyte-sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score, American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) grade, Kirkaldy-Willis functional grade, recurrence, and complications. Results The cohort included 7 male and 8 female patients, with a mean age of 32.9 ± 13.8 years. The diagnosis was supported by CT and MRI findings (all patients), positive T-SPOT results (13 patients), positive culture (8 patients), and histopathological confirmation (4 patients). Twelve patients required surgery, and 3 received conservative anti-TB therapy alone. The mean follow-up was 66.4 ± 4.4 months. ESR, CRP, and VAS scores decreased significantly after treatment. Among 9 patients with baseline neurological impairment, 8 improved by at least one ASIA grade; no patient deteriorated neurologically. No recurrence, vertebral body involvement, progressive kyphosis, implant failure, or deep infection was observed. Kirkaldy-Willis outcomes were excellent in 11 patients, good in 3, and fair in 1. Conclusion Isolated posterior element TB may be missed on plain radiographs. CT and MRI are essential for diagnosis. Anti-TB chemotherapy is fundamental, and surgery may be appropriate for selected patients with neurological deterioration, epidural abscess, sequestrum, large dorsal muscle abscess, or spinal instability.

title: Ultrasound Deep Learning for Distinguishing Benign Reactive from Hematologic Malignancy-Associated Cervical Lymphadenopathy in Children: Development and Validation
abstract: Abstract Background Cervical lymphadenopathy is a common reason for pediatric outpatient visits. It is usually reactive but may also accompany leukemia or lymphoma. Because these conditions may have overlapping ultrasound appearances, we developed a deep-learning model to distinguish benign reactive from hematologic malignancy-associated cervical lymphadenopathy. The model may provide valuable support for diagnosing hematologic malignancies and guiding differential diagnosis in pediatric outpatient practice. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 653 cervical lymph-node annotations after four duplicate images with discordant diagnoses were excluded. The benign reactive group comprised 283 annotations, and the hematologic malignancy-associated group comprised 370. Related images were kept in the same data fold, yielding 559 non-redundant image groups for analysis. An ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNetV2-S model using consensus lesion masks was evaluated with grouped nested five-fold cross-validation. Model probabilities were calibrated with Platt scaling. The primary endpoint was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and the Brier score were also assessed. Results The model achieved an AUC of 0.863 (95% confidence interval, 0.834 to 0.893) and an average precision of 0.865. At the Youden operating point, accuracy was 0.784, sensitivity was 0.773, specificity was 0.796, and positive predictive value was 0.824. The calibrated Brier score was 0.154. AUCs for the four diagnosis-specific comparisons ranged from 0.839 to 0.883. Conclusions Ultrasound image analysis showed good internal discrimination between benign reactive and hematologic malignancy-associated cervical lymphadenopathy in children. These findings support multicenter, patient-level evaluation of the model as an adjunct to ultrasound assessment.This model could provide radiologists and other clinicians with decision support for the non-invasive ultrasound assessment of cervical lymphadenopathy in children.

title: MVMGNN: Multi-View Masked Graph Neural Network for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis using Structural MRI
abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, and early diagnosis is essential for timely intervention. Structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) provides valuable information for characterizing AD-related brain alterations. However, existing sMRI-based brain graph methods often rely on single graph construction strategies, limiting their ability to capture complementary spatial and morphological relationships among brain regions. Moreover, multi-view approaches may introduce redundant features and noisy connections without effective selection and fusion mechanisms.To address these issues, we propose a Multi-View Masked Graph Neural Network (MVMGNN) for AD diagnosis using sMRI data. Brain regions are represented as graph nodes with radiomics features, and two complementary graph views are constructed based on spatial proximity and feature similarity. A joint node–edge masking mechanism is introduced to adaptively select informative feature dimensions and structural connections. In addition, a patient-level cross-view gated fusion module is developed to integrate multi-view representations. Experimental results on the ADNI dataset demonstrate that MVMGNN achieves competitive performance compared with existing methods across AD-related classification tasks. Interpretability analysis further reveals discriminative brain regions and structural connections associated with AD, providing insights into sMRI-based brain network analysis.

title: Germline Whole-Gene Deletion of SDHA in a Carotid Body Paraganglioma Identified by Whole-Genome Sequencing and Confirmed by MLPA: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background : Carotid body paragangliomas are frequently associated with germline variants in succinate dehydrogenase ( SDH ) genes. Among these, SDHA variants are particularly challenging to diagnose due to low penetrance and the presence of highly homologous pseudogenes. Standard diagnostic workflows, including whole-exome sequencing and targeted panels, often fail to detect large structural variants, such as whole-gene deletions, leading to potential underdiagnosis. This case is the first to report a germline whole-gene deletion of SDHA identified via whole-genome sequencing (WGS), providing definitive physical evidence of the Knudson two-hit hypothesis through the somatic loss of the remaining allele in the tumor tissue. Case presentation : A 63-year-old female presented with a 2-cm, left carotid body tumor. There was no relevant family history. The tumor was successfully resected, and histopathology confirmed a paraganglioma. While immunohistochemistry showed a loss of both SDHA and SDHB expression, WGS of peripheral blood revealed what is, to our knowledge, the first reported germline whole-gene deletion of the SDHA gene (copy number ≈ 1.1) in the region chr5:210,651–314,171. Notably, this type of large structural variant is potentially elusive to standard genetic analysis workflows. Subsequent WGS of the tumor tissue confirmed biallelic inactivation through the loss of the remaining allele (copy number ≈ 0.86), representing a classic two-hit mechanism. This large-scale deletion of all SDHA exons was further validated using multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA), confirming it as the pathogenic driver. The patient remains under rigorous long-term follow-up given the reported 15% risk of malignancy associated with SDHA variants. Conclusions : This case highlights the clinical utility of WGS in overcoming the inherent limitations of exome-based sequencing for SDHA analysis. When clinical suspicion remains high - specifically in cases with SDHA-negative immunohistochemistry but negative standard genetic testing - WGS or MLPA should be employed to detect hidden structural variants. Accurate molecular diagnosis is essential not only for understanding the mechanism of tumorigenesis but also for tailoring oncological surveillance and genetic counseling for the patient and their family.

title: Vision Foundation Models for Multi-Modal Medical Image Classification
abstract: Abstract Clinicians combine several imaging modalities to reach a diagnosis. Yet assembling large annotated datasets for every modality combination is rarely feasible, and modalities are frequently missing in practice. Vision foundation models (FMs) could ease both problems by transferring from few labels, but this has mainly been shown for single images. We therefore compare FM initialisation (DINOv2 and MedSigLIP) against random initialisation, across fusion and training strategies, on three tasks: glioma subtyping from multi-sequence MRI, HER2 scoring from paired histopathology stains, and liver-lesion classification from multi-phase MRI. At full data, FM initialisation matched or outperformed random initialisation, raising liver-lesion sensitivity from 54 % to 76 %. The advantage held as labels grew scarce and was largest under missing modalities, where FM initialisation kept sensitivity near 73 % as random initialisation fell to 29 %. For multi-modal medical imaging, FM initialisation is a strong default, most valuable when labels are scarce or acquisition protocols incomplete.

title: D3Seg: Dependency-Aware Diffusion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing Modalities
abstract: Abstract Accurate brain tumor segmentation using multi-parametric MRI is critical for effective treatment planning. However, in clinical settings, complete acquisition of all MRI sequences is not always possible. The absence of certain MRI modalities results in substantial performance degradation in existing segmentation methods, which typically rely on naive feature concatenation or direct fusion strategies. To address this limitation, we propose a novel segmentation model D 3 Seg which is designed to maintain stable performance under missing-modality settings. D 3 Seg introduces Multi-hop Modality Graph Fusion (MMGF) to model higher-order inter-modality dependencies, a lightweight diffusion-based imputation mechanism to compensate for missing T1ce and FLAIR feature representations in latent space, and probability-space decision refinement to mitigate dominant-class overconfidence and improve delineation of underrepresented tumor subregions. We evaluate the proposed D 3 Seg model on BraTS 2023 Glioma as the primary benchmark and further test it on a subset of the external BraTS 2023 Meningioma cohort to assess generalization across tumor pathologies.The results are compared with the state-of-the-art models under different missing-modality conditions. The proposed model achieves approximately 1.5–2.0% Dice improvement on enhancing tumor (ET) and around 1.0% on tumor core (TC) across multiple missing-modality configurations compared to the current state-of-the-art model on BraTS Glioma dataset. Cross-cohort evaluation on BraTS Meningioma dataset demonstrates the generalizability of the proposed model, showing consistent improvements in the challenging TC and ET regions, with approximately 1.5-3.0% and 1.5-6.5% gains respectively across several missing-modality configurations.

title: Possible Neurosarcoidosis Presenting with Chronic Pachymeningeal Disease, Extensive Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis, and Recurrent Seizures: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Neurosarcoidosis is an uncommon manifestation of sarcoidosis that can involve the meninges, cranial nerves, brain parenchyma, spinal cord, and cerebral vasculature. Its clinical and radiological manifestations frequently overlap with infectious, inflammatory, neoplastic, and vascular disorders, creating substantial diagnostic challenges. Case presentation: A 42-year-old woman presented with recurrent abnormal involuntary movements and progressive neurological deterioration. Her illness had evolved over approximately 12 years, beginning with chronic headache followed by right periorbital discomfort, progressive visual impairment, facial sensory symptoms, and later progressive focal neurological deficits. She was initially evaluated for a brain tumor and subsequently received prolonged anti-tuberculous therapy on more than one occasion for presumed tuberculous meningitis, with incomplete or absent clinical response. Over the months preceding the current admission, she developed progressive hemiparesis, abnormal posturing, facial twitching, dysarthria, urinary symptoms, and recurrent focal seizures that subsequently became prolonged and generalized with impaired consciousness. Serial brain imaging reported chronic pachymeningeal and leptomeningeal enhancement, cortical and subcortical abnormalities, features of raised intracranial pressure, and progressive vascular complications. Contrast-enhanced CT subsequently demonstrated superior sagittal sinus and bilateral cavernous sinus thrombosis with multifocal cerebral venous infarction/edema and small bilateral hemispheric and tentorial/interhemispheric subdural hematomas. Laboratory evaluation did not demonstrate a clear alternative infectious or systemic autoimmune etiology. A skin punch biopsy of healed chest lesions showed a sclerosing/keloidal scar without histological evidence of sarcoidosis or tuberculosis. Abdominopelvic ultrasonography additionally demonstrated chronic portal vein occlusion/thrombosis with periportal collateral vessels and periportal fibrosis. title: Functional-Structural Dissociation in Acute Stroke: Multi-Layered Lurian Syndromic Analysis and Network Hub Disruption
abstract: Abstract Background Acute cerebral ischemia presents a critical dissociation between hyperacute synaptic failure and macrostructural tissue necrosis. Conventional linear screening instruments (e.g., MMSE, MoCA) exhibit pronounced ceiling effects and obscure modular neurodynamic disconnection. Modern connectomics posits that focal ischemia triggers acute network diaschisis across distributed large-scale circuits—specifically the default mode and frontoparietal control networks – prior to the emergence of radiologically visible cytotoxic edema on non-contrast computed tomography (CT). We evaluated a digital adaptation of Luria’s qualitative syndromic process approach to quantify this functional-structural dissociation during early post-stroke triage. Methods In this observational audit at a tertiary stroke center, 124 patients with verified acute stroke were stratified by emergent neuroimaging into an acute CT-negative presentation group (n = 56) and a macrostructural lesion-verified necrosis group (n = 68). Bedside neuropsychological testing (24–48 hours post-ICU stabilization) was conducted via the NeuroDraft platform across 10 independent cognitive domains using the continuous Luria Raw metric (0.0–5.0 penalty scale). Latent dimensionality was examined via complete-case Principal Component Analysis (PCA) with orthogonal Varimax rotation (n = 121), following the predefined methodological exclusion of 3 individuals with early-stage extrapyramidal pathology to prevent motor-slowing confounds. Results Memory and attention deficits exhibited striking cross-cohort statistical equivalence. Memory impairment showed near-identical severity (M = 1.69 ± 0.91 vs. 1.80 ± 0.93; U = 1870.5, p = 0.87), and complex attention diverged minimally (M = 1.19 ± 0.95 vs. 1.43 ± 0.94; U = 1677.0, p = 0.25), demonstrating early network-level vulnerability preceding macroscopic cytotoxic alterations. Conversely, language functions demonstrated significant resilience in the CT-negative cohort (M = 0.69 ± 0.98 vs. 1.14 ± 1.20; U = 1465.5, p = 0.03). Intra-individual profile variability revealed a trend toward syndromic flattening as structural damage consolidated (coefficient of variation: 1.26 vs. 1.09; U = 1344.0, p = 0.06). Factor decomposition resolved two independent axes: posterior instrumental-operational integrity and anterior-subcortical dynamic-regulatory control. Conclusions Network-level functional collapse outpaces visible parenchymal necrosis in emergent stroke. Digital Lurian profiling provides sensitive, deterministic quantification of early diaschisis, supporting bedside decision-making without replacing macrostructural neuroimaging.

title: Analyzing the Prognostic Value of Radiomic Variables from PET-CT with [18F]FDG in a Retrospective Cohort of Patients with Adrenocortical Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate whether radiomic features extracted from [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT are associated with established prognostic factors and survival outcomes in patients with adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) in an exploratory proof-of-concept study. Methods In this retrospective study, 22 patients with histologically confirmed ACC who underwent pretreatment [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT were included. Conventional PET metrics (SUVmax, SUVmean, MTV, and TLG) and radiomic features were extracted. Dimensionality reduction was performed using principal component analysis (PCA). Machine learning models were developed to predict 5-year survival. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC). Associations between imaging parameters and clinical-pathological variables were evaluated statistically. Results Interobserver agreement for tumor segmentation was high (mean DSC = 86.2% ± 6.0%). The Naive Bayes model based on both PET and CT data achieved the highest accuracy among all other models (AUC = 0.750). Conventional PET parameters were not significantly correlated with Ki-67 or Weiss score; however, higher TLG had a non-significant association with p53-positive tumors in this small sample (p = 0.065). Conclusions Radiomic features derived from [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT demonstrate potential prognostic value in ACC. PET-based models outperformed CT-based models. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Ultrasound-Intensified Solvent-Free Lipase-Catalyzed Synthesis of 2-Phenethyl Octanoate: Molecular Docking and ANN-Based Process Optimization
abstract: Abstract 2-Phenethyl octanoate (2-PO) is a food flavoring ester with a mild fruity, wine-like odor. This paper introduces an ultrasound-intensified solvent-free lipase-catalyzed process for 2-PO synthesis from 2-phenylethanol and octanoic acid using Novozym® 435. Under ANN-optimized conditions, the process achieved 87.01% molar conversion within 6.48 min, versus 45.84 ± 2.66% without ultrasound, confirming its benefit in the solvent-free system. ANN modeling (R² = 0.9974, RMSE = 0.5535) outperformed response surface methodology (RSM; R² = 0.9333, RMSE = 4.1984) in capturing nonlinear variable interactions, with a predicted optimum of 88.16% validated experimentally as 87.01 ± 1.02%. Docking analysis supported substrate positioning within the Ser105–His224–Asp187 catalytic triad, while the stronger predicted binding affinity of 2-PO (− 6.524 kcal/mol) may explain the product-associated active-site occupancy and kinetic plateau observed. Green metrics confirmed process sustainability, with an E-factor of 0.49 kg/kg and atom economy of 93.24%, reflecting minimal waste in the solvent-free system. After 10 cycles, Novozym® 435 retained 88.8% of its initial molar conversion, indicating operational stability. These findings establish a docking-guided, ultrasound-assisted framework for the scalable, sustainable biosynthesis of food-grade aromatic esters for natural flavor applications.

title: Regional Gray Matter Volume Differences and Clinical Correlates in Anorexia Nervosa
abstract: Abstract Objective Structural MRI findings in anorexia nervosa are widespread, but the regional pattern and its clinical and neurochemical meaning remain incompletely defined. Methods We analyzed T1 weighted MRI and clinical data from the BEACON and SCAN datasets, including 122 participants with anorexia nervosa and 128 healthy controls. Gray matter volume was extracted for 163 AAL3 regions and compared between groups with models adjusted for age, total intracranial volume and cohort. Within the anorexia nervosa group, partial Spearman correlations and restricted cubic splines assessed relationships of diagnosis selected regions with body mass index, eating disorder symptoms and affective symptoms. The pooled diagnostic contrast was also compared with 39 normative PET and SPECT maps across 148 AAL3 regions using spatial null permutations. Results Anorexia nervosa was associated with lower gray matter volume in the right olfactory cortex, left olfactory cortex and left inferior parietal gyrus. The adjusted differences were 0.0421, 0.0417 and 0.3209 mL in magnitude, with q values from 0.0210 to 0.0268. Effects had the same direction in both cohorts, although no region survived correction within either cohort alone. Partial rank correlations were not significant. Restricted cubic splines identified nonlinear associations of left inferior parietal volume with body mass index and dietary restraint. The diagnostic t map showed negative spatial correlations with normative mGluR5, SV2A, GABAa and 5 HT2A maps. Conclusion These results localize a reproducible structural pattern while separating diagnostic anatomy from clinical variation and normative neurochemical organization, providing specific targets for longitudinal and multimodal studies of anorexia nervosa.

title: Diagnostic Value of Peripheral Zone PSA Density for Detecting Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer in Men with Peripheral Zone MRI Lesions Running title: Peripheral Zone PSA Density in Prostate Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Whole-gland prostate-specific antigen density (PSAD) may underestimate the diagnostic contribution of peripheral zone (PZ) tumors, as it is diluted by transition zone (TZ) volume, which expands with age independent of cancer risk. We investigated whether PZ-specific PSAD (PSAD_PZ) improves the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) in men with PZ-only multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) target lesions, and evaluated the analogous TZ-specific PSAD (PSAD_TZ) in men with TZ-only targets. Methods We analyzed 651 men from the prospectively enrolled SUPER-PC registry, supplemented by a retrospectively identified non-cancer cohort, who underwent combined systematic and MRI-targeted fusion biopsy (416 with PZ-only and 235 with TZ-only mpMRI targets). Clinically significant prostate cancer was defined as International Society of Urological Pathology Grade Group 2 or greater. The diagnostic performance of PSA, whole-gland PSAD, and zone-specific PSAD was compared using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and optimal cut-off values were determined using the Youden index. Results In the PZ-target group, PSAD_PZ achieved a significantly higher area under the curve (AUC) than PSA (0.825 vs. 0.707, p < 0.001) and whole-gland PSAD (0.825 vs. 0.702, p < 0.001). This advantage persisted among men with Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) category 4 or higher lesions (AUC 0.842) and remained significant after multivariable adjustment. The optimal PSAD_PZ cut-off value was 0.285 ng/mL/cm³, yielding a sensitivity of 70.8% and specificity of 84.3%. PSAD_TZ did not outperform PSA or whole-gland PSAD in the TZ-target group. Conclusions PSAD_PZ improves the detection of csPCa in men with PZ-only mpMRI targets and outperforms conventional whole-gland PSAD, supporting a zone-matched normalization strategy that may help reduce unnecessary biopsies and guide treatment decisions. PSAD_TZ conferred no comparable benefit among men with TZ-only targets.

title: Toward Risk-Aware Clinical Decision Support in Gastrointestinal Endoscopy: A Tunable Asymmetric Loss with Uncertainty-Guided Referral
abstract: Abstract This study presents a deep learning framework for four-class gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy risk stratification beyond conventional binary lesion detection. Im- ages from the HyperKvasir dataset were categorized into four clinically motivated risk groups: Normal, Inflammatory, Pre-malignant, and High-Risk, informed by rec- ommendations from the American College of Gastroenterology and European Soci- ety of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy. We introduce an Asymmetric Endoscopy Loss (AEL) function that enables tunable class weighting, allowing greater emphasis on High-Risk cases while balancing overall predictive performance with safety-oriented sensitivity. Three lightweight architectures (DenseNet-121, EfficientNet-B0, and DeiT-Tiny) were evaluated using AEL, with Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty estimation and a referral strategy that escalates Pre-malignant and High-Risk pre- dictions for further review regardless of model confidence. GradCAM was used to provide visual interpretability. DenseNet-121 achieved a macro F1-score of 0.8419 and an AUC of 0.9730. No ground-truth High-Risk images were predicted as either of the two lower-risk tiers on the internal test set, and 43.1 % of images were eligi- ble for simulated automatic clearance under the predefined referral rule. Five-fold cross-validation provided an additional assessment of performance stability, while McNemar tests quantified paired differences between architectures. These findings support further investigation of tunable risk-weighted losses, lightweight architec- tures, and uncertainty-aware referral strategies for developing interpretable and safety-oriented GI endoscopy decision-support systems.

title: CT Colonography as a Triage Examination After a Positive Fecal Immunochemical Test: A Retrospective Cohort Study in a Chilean Screening Program
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To evaluate computed tomography colonography (CTC) as a triage examination for colonoscopy within a fecal immunochemical test (FIT)-based colorectal cancer screening program in a resource-limited region of Chile. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included asymptomatic FIT-positive individuals aged 45–75 years who underwent CTC between January 2019 and November 2022. Patients with CT Colonography Reporting and Data System (C-RADS) C2–C4 findings were referred for optical colonoscopy. The primary outcome was the per-patient positive predictive value (PPV) of CTC for polyps measuring ≥ 6 mm among patients with an evaluable colonoscopy. Results: The cohort comprised 675 patients (mean age 64.0 years, SD 9.2; 443 women, 65.6%). Overall, 473 patients (70.1%) were classified as C1 and were not referred for immediate colonoscopy, 62 (9.2%) had C3–C4 findings and 71 (10.5%) had unresolved C0 examinations. Of 131 patients referred for colonoscopy, 115 (87.8%) underwent the procedure and 108 had an evaluable examination. Colonoscopy confirmed at least one polyp measuring ≥ 6 mm in 93 patients, yielding a PPV of 86.1% (95% CI 78.3–91.4). Advanced colorectal neoplasia was confirmed in 48 patients (PPV 44.4%, 95% CI 35.4–53.8). The detection rates was 42/675 (6.2%) for advanced adenoma and 6/675 (0.9%) for colorectal cancer. Conclusion: Among FIT-positive patients with CTC findings warranting colonoscopy, clinically relevant colorectal lesions were frequently confirmed. CTC may help prioritize colonoscopy in settings with limited endoscopic capacity. Further evaluation of the complete screening pathway is warranted.

title: Key performance indicators for organized risk stratified prostate cancer screening in Europe: first results from the PRAISE-U and EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing programme
abstract: Abstract Background. Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer in men in the European Union. Following the 2022 Council Recommendation to evaluate organised screening based on prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), PRAISE-U defined 21 harmonised key performance indicators (KPIs). We report their first empirical values from the five PRAISE-U pilots and, through a common survey, from EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing (OPT) programme. Methods. In PRAISE-U, men aged 50–69 years at five pilot sites in Spain, Lithuania, Poland and Ireland were invited to risk-stratified screening comprising PSA testing, first-level risk stratification, MRI for intermediate or high risk and selective biopsy, with prospective capture in a central REDCap database. EUCanScreen pilots and the Swedish organised prostate cancer testing (OPT) programme reported the same KPIs through an online survey. Results. Twelve programmes reported KPI values. Across the five PRAISE-U pilots, participation ranged from 7.1% to 43.0%, PSA exceeded 3 ng/ml in 9.2–15.0%, and compliance was 76.4–96.0% for first-level risk assessment, 89.9–98.3% for MRI and 78.9–99.0% for biopsy. Detection ranged from 8 to 26 per 1,000 screened in PRAISE-U and from 4.3 to 28 across all programmes. ISUP grade 1 accounted for 20.3–81.4% of cancers, active-surveillance uptake for 14.8–100%, and mean time from PSA result to MRI for 19–114 days; external values fell broadly within the PRAISE-U ranges. Thirteen of 21 KPIs were fully reported by all five pilots, all describing the diagnostic pathway; retention and the three impact indicators were reported only by Sweden, which reported 19 of 21. Conclusions. Diagnostic-pathway KPIs were measurable under pilot conditions, whereas programme-level indicators required a defined target population or registry linkage. Sweden, the only population-based programme, reported retention and long-term impact, identifying the infrastructure needed before organised PCa screening can be monitored at scale.

Detection ranged from 8 to 26 per 1,000 screened in PRAISE-U and from 4.3 to 28 across all programmes. ISUP grade 1 accounted for 20.3–81.4% of cancers, active-surveillance uptake for 14.8–100%, and mean time from PSA result to MRI for 19–114 days; external values fell broadly within the PRAISE-U ranges. Thirteen of 21 KPIs were fully reported by all five pilots, all describing the diagnostic pathway; retention and the three impact indicators were reported only by Sweden, which reported 19 of 21. Conclusions. Diagnostic-pathway KPIs were measurable under pilot conditions, whereas programme-level indicators required a defined target population or registry linkage. Sweden, the only population-based programme, reported retention and long-term impact, identifying the infrastructure needed before organised PCa screening can be monitored at scale.

title: Ethmoidal alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma with orbital extension in a young adult: A case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is an uncommon malignant neoplasm of skeletal muscle differentiation that predominantly affects children. Sinonasal RMS is rare in adults, and the alveolar subtype tends toward aggressive local growth with regional and distant spread. Its clinical and radiologic presentation can overlap with inflammatory, infectious, and other malignant sinonasal processes, which makes diagnosis difficult. Case presentation A 28-year-old Middle Eastern man presented with a one-week history of right-sided proptosis and right eye pain, associated with diplopia and painful upward gaze but without prominent sinonasal symptoms. Computed tomography demonstrated a heterogeneous expansile mass centered in the right ethmoid and maxillary sinuses with extension through the lamina papyracea into the right orbit. Endoscopic sinus surgery with tumor debulking and biopsy demonstrated erosion of the lamina papyracea and extensive involvement of the ethmoid air cells. Histopathology showed an infiltrative malignant small round blue cell neoplasm arranged in nests and lobules separated by delicate fibrovascular stroma, with brisk mitotic activity, including seven mitotic figures per high-power field. Tumor cells showed diffuse strong nuclear expression of myogenin and MyoD1 and retained INI1. Pan-cytokeratin, CK5/6, chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100, CD99, FLI1, CD20, and CD3 were negative. Molecular testing was positive for FOXO1 rearrangement, supporting the diagnosis of alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma. Staging demonstrated no definite distant metastatic disease. Systemic chemotherapy with ifosfamide and etoposide was initiated, and the patient remains under treatment and follow-up. Conclusion Adult sinonasal alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is rare and can be difficult to diagnose; it may present with orbital manifestations despite limited sinonasal symptoms. Its characteristic morphology, myogenic immunophenotype, and FOXO1 rearrangement help establish the diagnosis. Management requires a multidisciplinary team and careful evaluation of orbital and intracranial extension.

title: Sonographic Appearance of Congenital Cervical Teratoma: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background : Cervical teratomas account for only 3–9% of neonatal teratomas. Although usually benign, they may cause significant airway compression, necessitating prompt diagnosis and surgical intervention. Cervical teratomas are typically cystic or cystic-solid and often contain calcifications; a predominantly solid, hypervascular mass without calcification is rare and may pose a diagnostic challenge. We report such a case to highlight its atypical sonographic features and the diagnostic value of combining ultrasound with color Doppler imaging and ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (FNA). Case presentation : A six-hour-old female neonate was transferred for respiratory distress after tracheal intubation. Physical examination revealed a firm midline cervical mass (4×3×5cm). Ultrasonography showed a predominantly solid, heterogeneously echogenic mass with irregular margins and increased vascularity. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated mild enhancement with tracheal displacement, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed tracheal compression. Ultrasound-guided FNA yielded fibrous and cartilaginous elements, supporting the diagnosis of teratoma. The tumor was surgically resected, and histopathology confirmed a mature solid teratoma. Conclusions : Cervical teratomas may present atypically as predominantly solid, hypervascular masses without detectable calcification. In neonates with respiratory distress and a cervical mass, prompt diagnosis and surgery are imperative. Ultrasonography combined with color Doppler imaging and FNA provides valuable preoperative information for surgical decision-making.

title: OpenWell: Energy-Based Interactive Discovery for Open-World Medical Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Volumetric medical segmentation typically relies on closed-set assumptions, failing to identify or adapt to anatomical anomalies outside a fixed training vocabulary. We propose OpenWell , an energy-based framework that bridges the gap between Open-World discovery and interactive adaptation. Unlike deterministic approaches, OpenWell models anatomical classes as probabilistic energy wells on the hypersphere, using von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distributions. This formulation captures both the semantic identity and intra-class uncertainty of tissues, enabling out-of-distribution detection via a Free Energy score. Furthermore, we introduce an Instant Enrollment mechanism: triggered by a single user interaction, the system initializes a new energy well, allowing the model to adapt to previously unseen structures in real-time without gradient-based retraining. Extensive evaluations on AMOS, BTCV, MSD-Pancreas, and TotalSegmentator-MRI demonstrate that OpenWell improves Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection AUROC over closed-set and foundation models, while achieving rapid, one-shot interactive adaptation to novel classes.
