title: Automated Gleason Grading and Prostate Cancer Classification from Histopathology Images: A Systematic Review of Deep Learning Models, Generalizability, Failure Modes, and Challenges in Low-Resource Settings
abstract: Abstract Background Digital pathology and deep learning have produced rapid advances in automated prostate cancer detection and Gleason grading. However, headline performance from internal benchmark datasets does not necessarily translate to reliable clinical performance across institutions, scanners, staining protocols, specimen types, or patient populations. This review synthesizes evidence on automated Gleason grading and prostate cancer classification from histopathology images, with particular emphasis on external validation, generalizability, failure modes, human–AI interaction, and deployment in low-resource settings. Methods The review was structured according to PRISMA 2020 principles. PubMed-indexed studies, publisher records, systematic reviews, and methodological guidance were examined, with emphasis on original studies of digital histopathology AI for prostate cancer and Gleason grading. Fifty key publications were selected for the evidence synthesis, supplemented conceptually by broader literature identified in prior systematic reviews. Because the evidence is heterogeneous in specimen type, endpoint, annotation strategy, architecture, and validation design, a narrative synthesis was used rather than an unverified pooled estimate. Results The evidence demonstrates that deep learning can approach or exceed the agreement of general pathologists and can achieve expert-level performance in selected external cohorts. The PANDA challenge demonstrated strong cross-continental performance using 10,616 digitized prostate biopsies, while subsequent real-world evaluations showed wider performance variation among algorithms. External validation on prostatectomy specimens has also demonstrated strong agreement for a biopsy-trained commercial model. Prospective multicenter evidence published in 2026 indicates that AI assistance can alter Gleason grading in routine practice and increase diagnostic confidence. Persistent weaknesses include domain shift, tissue and scanning artifacts, class imbalance, difficulty distinguishing adjacent Gleason patterns, limited prospective validation, dataset leakage, opaque reference standards, and underrepresentation of low-resource settings. Conclusion AI-assisted prostate histopathology has moved beyond proof-of-concept research, but clinical readiness should not be inferred from accuracy on a single dataset. Future studies should prioritize independent multicenter validation, prespecified clinical endpoints, transparent reference standards, calibration and uncertainty reporting, robustness testing, prospective workflow studies, and implementation strategies compatible with low-resource pathology laboratories.

title: Umbilical Cord Hernia is Not an Isolated Pathology: High Rate of Associated Anomalies in a Tertiary Center Cohort
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile of umbilical cord hernia (UCH), a defect often considered a minor variant of omphalocele, with a specific focus on the prevalence and spectrum of associated congenital anomalies. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 45 neonates with anterior abdominal wall defects treated between August 2019 and July 2024. Patients were categorized into three groups: omphalocele (n = 15), gastroschisis (n = 19), and UCH (n = 11). Demographic data, prenatal diagnosis, associated anomalies, surgical management, and outcomes were analyzed. Results In the UCH group, six patients (54.5%) had at least one major associated anomaly. Major cardiac anomalies were present in 45.5% (5/11), chromosomal anomalies in 27.3% (3/11), and genitourinary anomalies in 36.4% (4/11) of patients. The spectrum included Tetralogy of Fallot, Trisomy 13, 18, 21, and genetic syndromes (e.g., 3MC syndrome). Four patients (36.4%) had isolated UCH. Mortality in the UCH group was 18.2%, exclusively occurring in patients with major associated anomalies. Conclusion Contrary to traditional belief, umbilical cord hernia is frequently associated with serious cardiac, chromosomal, and multisystemic anomalies. These findings necessitate a paradigm shift in management, advocating for comprehensive screening including echocardiography, renal ultrasound, and genetic evaluation in all neonates with UCH, similar to the standard for omphalocele.

title: When One View Isn’t Enough: Multimodal Cardiac Representation Fusion for Sudden Cardiac Arrest Risk
abstract: Abstract Risk of sudden cardiac arrest may be expressed differently by anatomy, mechanical function and electrical activity, while studies that contain all three modalities for the same patient are uncommon. We developed CardiacGuard-Net, a modular deep-learning framework that learns modality-specific representations from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), echocardiography and twelve-lead electrocardiography (ECG), then combines them for cardiac-arrest classification. The modality-specific models achieved mean Dice 0.953 for CMR segmentation, 3.8% mean absolute error for echocardiographic ejection-fraction estimation and AUC 0.938 for 24-h arrest prediction from ECG. For multimodal evaluation, 1,204 records were assembled into a matched benchmark using age band, sex, ejection-fraction band and diagnostic category because no dataset available to the study contained all three modalities for the same patients. On this benchmark, CardiacFusion-Net achieved AUC 0.947, compared with 0.920 for late fusion. Removing the ECG, CMR or echocardiographic branch reduced AUC by 0.035, 0.026 and 0.016, respectively. A single trained model also retained discrimination when modalities were withheld, with AUCs of 0.890 for ECG alone, 0.905 for MRI+echo, 0.921 for MRI + ECG and 0.931 for echo + ECG. The multimodal results are therefore best interpreted as an internal proof-of-concept benchmark of complementary information, not as patient-level clinical validation.

title: 18F-FDG PET/CT for Differentiating Reactive Lymphadenopathy, Lymphoma, and Tuberculosis in People Living with HIV
abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic contribution of 2-deoxy-2-[¹⁸F]fluoro-D-glucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT) metabolic, volumetric, and morphological parameters in differentiating human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-related reactive lymphadenopathy (LAP), lymphoma, and tuberculosis (TB) in people living with HIV. Methods PET/CT images of 96 patients with HIV (2010–2025) with reactive LAP (n = 67), lymphoma (n = 16), or TB (n = 13) were retrospectively reviewed. Maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), SUVmax-to-liver ratio (SURmax), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), nodal morphology, extranodal involvement, and maximum-intensity-projection (MIP) symmetry were compared among groups, and the association of antiretroviral therapy (ART) exposure with PET/CT parameters was assessed within the reactive LAP group. Results SUVmax and SURmax were significantly lower in reactive LAP than in lymphoma and TB (p < 0.001), with cut-offs of 16.46 (area under the curve [AUC] 0.959) and 3.83 (AUC 0.934) showing high discriminatory performance in distinguishing reactive LAP from lymphoma. MTV and TLG were higher in lymphoma and TB (p < 0.001). Symmetric MIP uptake was present in 98.5% of reactive LAP versus 56.2% of lymphoma and 46.2% of TB cases and was strongly associated with reactive LAP (p < 0.001). SUVmax, SURmax, MTV, and TLG were significantly lower in ART-experienced than ART-naïve reactive LAP patients (p < 0.001), and [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT guided biopsy target selection in 87.8% of biopsied patients. Conclusion [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT may aid differentiation of reactive lymphadenopathy from lymphoma and tuberculosis in people living with HIV through combined metabolic, volumetric, and morphological parameters — particularly MIP symmetry — and effectively guides biopsy planning. However, substantial overlap remains between lymphoma and tuberculosis.

title: ‘One shunt fits all?’: A comparative laboratory study of antibiotic- impregnated shunt catheters with retrospective clinical correlation
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Several antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters are commercially available, but direct comparative data on their biochemical and physical characteristics remain limited. Previous observations from our single-centre neurosurgical unit suggested that nominally similar catheter types may be associated with different rates of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain. We therefore conducted a prospective comparative study to investigate potential biochemical and physical differences between commercially available antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters. Methods: Ares®, Bactiseal® and XABO® catheters were compared for antibiotic content, rifampicin degradation products, elution characteristics and antimicrobial activity. Antibiotic elution was assessed during continuous saline perfusion at 20 mL/h and 37°C over 8 weeks, while antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis was evaluated over 60 days. Catheter dimensions, elastic modulus and surface morphology were assessed using three-dimensional computed tomography, nanoindentation and scanning electron microscopy, respectively. An exploratory retrospective quality-improvement dataset from our single-centre unit was additionally analysed to compare the frequency of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain between catheter types. Results: The three catheter systems showed product-specific differences in antibiotic content, rifampicin degradation profiles, elution characteristics, antimicrobial activity, dimensions, mechanical properties and surface morphology. XABO® most closely matched the declared antibiotic concentrations and retained the greatest proportion of intact rifampicin, while Ares® demonstrated the highest sustained clindamycin elution. All three catheters retained measurable activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis for 60 days, with XABO® showing the largest numerical inhibition zones throughout. In the 395-patient retrospective clinical analysis, otherwise unexplained abdominal pain was recorded in 90/182 patients with Ares® catheters (49.5%) compared with 12/108 patients with Bactiseal® catheters (11.1%). After adjustment for age, sex, primary diagnosis, modified Rankin Scale score and activity level, Ares® remained associated with greater odds of abdominal pain than Bactiseal® (adjusted OR 6.89, 95% CI 2.58–18.43; p<0.001). Conclusion: Commercially available antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters showed product-specific biochemical and physical variation, while catheter type was associated with different rates of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain in a retrospective single-centre analysis. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causality or clinical superiority. Prospective multicentre studies are required to determine whether catheter-specific properties translate into clinically meaningful differences and should influence individualised shunt selection.

title: 3D CT-GraphEdgeMAE: 3D CT Image Anomaly Detection Using Self-Supervised Graph Edge Mask Autoencoders
abstract: Abstract Computer tomography anomaly detection is the fastest and the most effective method of early diagnosing malignant tumor. Large scale training data, high computation, and excessive number of parameters demand abundant computing resources. We propose a new end-end 3D CT-GraphEdgeMAE to solve the 3D CT anomaly detection. We construct the graph for 3D CT to employ a standard encoder GCN to learn node feature, and crucially, propose a novel decoder which the Hadamard product and subgraph similarity are jointly used to predict the masked edges. Furthermore, we introduce a joint topology-aware contrastive-reconstruction loss function by constructing connected subgraph for two nodes of mask edge. We perform anomaly detection via graph node classification which can effectively captures both the characteristic fine-grained features and the gradual trend of lesions. Extensive experiments are conducted on the public 3D CT dateset LUNA16. Our method specifically tailored for training under small scale dateset，utilizes all 888 cases in LUNA16 and 88 case from a subset of LUNA16. On the downstream task of nodule detection, compared with MAE and other baselines, our method achieves a 30-fold reduction in training time and lowers computational cost by 68%, while attaining competitive FROC scores of 82.2% for 888 cases and 77.9% for 88 cases.

title: Operator-rated puncture performance and first-pass lesion tissue area in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: an exploratory single-center sub-analysis of endoscopic ultrasound- guided tissue acquisition
abstract: Abstract Background: Adequate tissue acquisition is important for histological assessment and ancillary testing in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). We primarily explored the association between operator-rated puncture performance and first-pass lesion tissue area during endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition (EUS-TA) in patients with PDAC. A secondary analysis examined whether this association was observed in the overall cohort, irrespective of final diagnosis. Methods: This exploratory single-center sub-analysis used prospective data from a multicenter randomized trial of 22-gauge fine-needle biopsy needles. Endoscopists rated overall puncture performance on a five-point scale after EUS-TA. Ratings were analyzed using two post hoc dichotomizations: very easy/easy versus indeterminate/difficult/very difficult, and very easy versus all other ratings. First-pass lesion tissue area was quantified automatically on histological slides using a digital microscope with image-analysis software. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations between ratings and tissue areas in each cohort, adjusting for needle type, puncture route, operator experience, and lesion size. Firth logistic regression assessed associations between ratings and exploratory ≥ 4-mm² benchmark attainment in the PDAC cohort. Trends in tissue area across very easy, easy, and remaining ratings were assessed using the Jonckheere–Terpstra test. Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) suitability was summarized descriptively. Results: Of 62 patients, 48 had PDAC. In the PDAC cohort, the very easy/easy comparison yielded inconclusive adjusted associations with tissue area and benchmark attainment. A very easy rating was associated with greater tissue area (median, 5.45 vs. 1.90 mm²; adjusted difference, 1.93 mm²; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.12–3.74) and benchmark attainment (57.7% vs. 22.7%; adjusted odds ratio, 4.44; 95% CI, 1.17–21.06). Tissue area decreased with less favorable ratings (p for trend = 0.016). Two of six patients assessed for CGP were considered suitable. In the overall cohort, lesion size remained associated with tissue area, whereas adjusted associations for both rating dichotomizations were inconclusive. Tissue area decreased with less favorable ratings (p for trend = 0.034). Conclusions: In patients with PDAC, an endoscopist’s very easy rating was associated with greater first-pass lesion tissue area after adjustment for lesion size and procedural factors. Prospective pass-by-pass studies are needed to validate this exploratory association and determine its utility in EUS-TA. Trial registration: Parent trial: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT), jRCT1042220099, registered on 25 November 2022.

title: Patient-level coronary artery disease classification from cardiac MRI using out-of-fold heart segmentation and same-slice region controls
abstract: Abstract Background Medical-image classifiers can obtain high apparent performance from correlated slices, acquisition patterns, or anatomy outside the intended target. The downloaded CAD Cardiac MRI Dataset release contained 63,425 JPEG images but only 30 independent top-level patient folders. This study evaluated whether cardiac-region representations were more informative than exact same-slice full-image and extra-cardiac controls under patient-level validation. Methods Each Directory_* folder was treated as one patient (16 Normal, 14 Sick), as confirmed by the dataset creator. The current analysis used five patient-level cross-fitted 2.5D Attention U-Nets trained from 5,097 accepted targets (3,949 heart-present and 1,148 no-heart). Every released image received an out-of-fold mask from a model that did not train on its patient. A frozen ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0 encoded full-image, cardiac-ROI, and exact-complement representations. Slice embeddings were averaged first within folder-defined series and then across series for each patient. Nested patient-level cross-validation evaluated eleven representations using exact same-slice controls, a secondary cross-class matched cohort, and paired patient-bootstrap intervals. Results The expanded manual-target state caused all five segmentation folds and all five out-of-fold prediction parts to be recomputed. Out-of-fold prediction produced 63,107 final-valid masks among 63,425 images; positive-target patient-balanced Dice was 0.809, and 73.4% of accepted no-heart targets received empty masks. On exactly 50,735 attention-eligible slices, the automatic cardiac ROI achieved AUC 0.938 (95% CI 0.847-1.000), compared with 0.830 for the full image and 0.772 for the complement. Paired AUC differences were 0.107 (95% CI 0.009–0.235) versus the full image and 0.165 (0.029–0.344) versus the complement. In the matched cohort, ROI AUC was 0.942, versus 0.821 for the full image and 0.741 for the complement. On the manual-positive subset, automatic and manual ROIs achieved AUCs of 0.973 and 0.951, respectively; their paired difference did not exclude zero. Conclusions After expanded manual annotation and a complete rerun of every dependent stage, out-of-fold cardiac localization retained an advantage over exact same-slice and matched controls. Complement AUCs of 0.741–0.835 nevertheless show substantial residual predictive information outside the intended cardiac region. With only 30 patients, no external validation, JPEG rather than DICOM data, and outcome-informed matching in a secondary analysis, these findings support a methodological proof of concept rather than clinical use.

title: Lesion-specific diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging compared with arthroscopy in chronic ankle pathologies with exploratory machine learning prediction
abstract: Abstract Background Understanding the diagnostic agreement between advanced imaging and arthroscopy is essential for accurate preoperative planning and tailored therapy. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic concordance between preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and direct arthroscopic examination for principal ankle pathologies and identify key predictors of arthroscopically confirmed osteochondral lesions (OLs) using machine learning (ML) predictive algorithms. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included 54 adults with chronic or recurrent ankle symptoms, who underwent preoperative imaging and subsequent ankle arthroscopy. Arthroscopy served as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, accuracy, and Cohen κ were calculated with 95% confidence intervals. Exploratory ML models predicting arthroscopically confirmed OLs were evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), followed by feature importance and ablation analyses. Results For OLs, MRI demonstrated 82.1% sensitivity, 80.8% specificity, 81.5% accuracy, and substantial agreement with arthroscopy (κ = 0.629). For synovitis, MRI showed 94.3% sensitivity and 100% specificity, although the specificity was based on only one arthroscopy-negative case. For loose body detection, MRI demonstrated 50.0% sensitivity and 90.5% specificity. For ligamentous injury, the sensitivity and specificity were 100% and 25.0%, respectively, with directional discordance between MRI and arthroscopy (exact McNemar P = 0.004). In the exploratory ML analysis, linear Support Vector Machine and Logistic Regression achieved LOOCV accuracies of 81.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Direct MRI visualization of the OL had the largest Logistic Regression feature weight (56.5%), and removing this feature reduced the Logistic Regression Accuracy to 50.0%. Conclusions MRI diagnostic performance varied according to lesion type, with balanced performance for OLs and high sensitivity for synovitis and ligamentous injury. Exploratory ML analysis indicated that direct MRI visualization was the predominant predictor of arthroscopically confirmed OLs, with smaller contributions from coexisting loose bodies and symptom duration. Preoperative MRI provides excellent accuracy and unbiased diagnostic agreement for OLs and synovitis and serves as an indispensable tool for surgical planning. However, clinicians should recognize the potential for discordance between MRI and arthroscopic findings in the assessment of ligamentous injury as well as the limited sensitivity of MRI for detecting small intra-articular loose bodies. Level of Evidence: Level 3

title: Synoptic procedural reporting to improve quality indicators in systematic Staging Endobronchial Ultrasound (EBUS) in Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): protocol for an ambispective multi-centre quality improvement study
abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate mediastinal staging by systematic staging endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) is essential for prognosticating and guiding management in curative-intent treatment in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Narrative procedural reports are often incomplete and inconsistent between clinicians, limiting assessment of procedural quality and meaningful audit. Synoptic (structured, check-list style) reporting has improved documentation completeness and procedural quality in other domains of medicine, and a recent Australian multicentre study demonstrated synoptic reporting significantly improved both report and procedural quality in staging EBUS. This ambispective, international, multicentre study aims to evaluate whether synoptic procedural reporting improves quality indicators of systematic staging EBUS, encompassing both process and outcome measures, and will assess acceptability and feasibility to proceduralists. Methods: This ambispective multicentre, single-arm interventional study will recruit approximately 15 lung cancer services with substantial EBUS procedural volume. Eligible patients will have known or suspected clinical stage IB-IIIC NSCLC undergoing systematic staging EBUS for treatment planning. Each centre will implement a mandated synoptic report requiring documentation for each of the five mediastinal lymph nodes: examination, size of node and biopsy details. Three months of staging procedures will be contributed prior to and following implementation of this reporting practice. The primary outcome is the proportion of patients with a complete staging procedure. Secondary outcomes include PET-occult lymph node metastases detection, nodes sampled, radiologically normal node sampling, inter-site variance, and proceduralist feasibility/acceptability. A sample of 590 patients (295 pre-, 295 post-intervention) provides 80% power to detect an 8% increase in complete staging. Mixed-effects logistic and Poisson regression, with random effect for centre and adjustment for pre-specified baseline case-mix covariates, will be used. Discussion: This study will provide the first international multicentre evaluation of whether synoptic reporting improves procedural completeness and clinically meaningful outcomes in systematic staging EBUS. Demonstrating improved complete staging procedures and PET-occult lymph node detection, with proceduralist acceptability, would support widespread adoption of synoptic reporting as a quality improvement tool, strengthen alignment with WABIP quality frameworks, reduce variance in care, and support more accurate multidisciplinary decision-making for NSCLC patients. Trial registration: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR), ACTRN12625001281482. Registered 18 November 2025. Retrospectively registered.

title: Sex differences in quantitative fundus parameters measured by artificial intelligence: a cross-sectional community study
abstract: Abstract Background Automated analysis of fundus photographs yields numerous quantitative measures, but sex differences in these measures and their modification by systemic conditions are not well characterized. We quantified these differences in a large community screening cohort. Methods This cross-sectional study included 21,844 participants contributing 32,576 eye-level records to a community health-screening program in Ganzhou, China. EVisionAI was used to quantify 49 vascular, optic disc and cup, peripapillary atrophy, and fundus tessellation density parameters from color fundus photographs. Generalized estimating equations clustered by participant estimated male-female differences in standardized parameters. Models were unadjusted, adjusted for age and age squared, and further adjusted for 20 binary systemic conditions. Sex-by-condition interactions were examined for 19 conditions; prostatic hyperplasia was assessed separately using a three-level variable. Benjamini–Hochberg correction was applied across all fundus parameters within each model for the primary comparisons and within each condition for the interaction analyses. Results Mean age was 63.6 ± 9.8 years in women and 63.9 ± 10.1 years in men. After full adjustment and FDR correction, sex differences were found in 41 of 49 parameters: 19 of 22 optic disc and cup, 8 of 11 vascular, 7 of 7 peripapillary atrophy, and 7 of 9 fundus tessellation density measures. The largest standardized differences in men were a lower disc vertical-to-horizontal ratio (β = −0.170; 95% confidence interval, − 0.196 to − 0.144) and a higher atrophy arc height-to-disc vertical diameter ratio (β = 0.166; 95% confidence interval, 0.141 to 0.192). The arteriole-to-venule ratio was also lower in men (β = −0.113; 95% confidence interval, − 0.137 to − 0.089). Estimates were generally stable across models. Twenty-three effect-modification findings remained significant after false discovery rate correction, predominantly involving prostatic hyperplasia. Conclusions Sex differences were present across most quantitative fundus parameters and changed little after adjustment for measured systemic conditions. Their relevance to screening requires validation in datasets with ocular biometry and clinical outcomes.

title: From detection to decision: radiographic predictors of clinical complications in 514 supernumerary teeth: A retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Supernumerary teeth exhibit various morphological characteristics and may lead to a range of complications. This study aimed to evaluate radiographic characteristics of supernumerary teeth in children and to determine associations with complications and treatment status. Materials and methods This study included 386 systemically healthy paediatric patients (5–15.9 years) with 514 supernumerary teeth identified on panoramic radiographs. Variables included number, location, morphology, eruption direction, eruption status, root development stage, and complications. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests, independent samples t-tests, and multivariable binary logistic and multinomial regression models. Results The mean age was 9.07 ± 2.08 years, and 70.2% of patients were male. Significant differences were observed between erupted and impacted teeth regarding morphology, eruption direction, root development stage, complications, and Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) use (p < 0.05). Morphology and root development stage were associated with complication patterns (p < 0.05). Multivariable regression analyses showed that CBCT use was associated with eruption status, dentition “stage, side distribution, and delayed eruption. Anterior maxillary localisation was strongly associated with conical and tuberculate morphologies. Midline location was associated with increased odds of both complete and partial root development (p < 0.001). Conclusion Supernumerary teeth exhibit distinct radiographic characteristics associated with clinical complications. Morphology, eruption status, and root development were associated with clinical and radiographic findings. Early radiographic evaluation is essential for individualised treatment planning.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Cervical Cancer Histopathology in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review of Segmentation, Classification Techniques, and Barriers to Deployment
abstract: Abstract Background and Objective Cervical cancer remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where access to pathology expertise, screening, tissue diagnosis and digital pathology infrastructure is uneven. Histopathological examination remains central to confirming cervical neoplasia, grading lesions and guiding management. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers opportunities to support pathologists by automating image segmentation and classification, but evidence on clinical generalisability and deployment in SSA is fragmented. This systematic review synthesizes AI techniques for cervical histopathology segmentation and classification and examines barriers to translation into routine practice in SSA. Methods A structured systematic evidence synthesis was prepared and reported with reference to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020). Contemporary evidence was identified from PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar searches and from reference chaining of relevant systematic reviews. Eligible evidence addressed cervical histopathology or closely related cervical image-analysis tasks involving segmentation, feature learning, classification, whole-slide analysis, clinical validation or deployment. The synthesis focused on 49 substantive publications spanning classical image processing, machine learning, CNNs, transfer learning, U-Net-family and other segmentation methods, attention/transformer models, whole-slide analysis, African studies and digital-pathology implementation. Results The evidence shows a transition from thresholding, clustering, watershed, active contours and handcrafted morphological/texture features toward CNN-based segmentation and classification, transfer learning, multiple-instance learning, attention models and transformer/foundation-model approaches. Early studies were frequently based on small, pre-segmented public datasets, whereas newer studies increasingly use histology images and whole-slide images. African evidence remains limited but is expanding. An Ethiopian study used 915 histopathology images and EfficientNetB0, reporting 94.5% test accuracy for cervical cancer classification. A 2026 Rwandan study used 885 patient-level H&E cervical biopsy images and reported EfficientNetB0 accuracy of 0.99 with ROC-AUC 0.99 on a held-out test set. A Ugandan study used 5,966 cervical histopathology images acquired with smartphone-assisted microscopy and DeepLabV3 + with a ResNet34 encoder for 21-feature segmentation, reporting validation mIoU of approximately 75.8% and Dice of approximately 93.1%. Conclusion AI has substantial potential to augment cervical histopathology in SSA, but reported algorithmic performance should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical readiness. The dominant evidence gaps are external validation, prospective evaluation, multi-institutional datasets, standardised staining and imaging, transparent reporting, calibration, explainability, workflow integration and implementation economics. Future research should prioritize locally representative datasets, lightweight and edge-capable models, patient-level validation, human-in-the-loop decision support and implementation studies conducted within African pathology workflows.

The dominant evidence gaps are external validation, prospective evaluation, multi-institutional datasets, standardised staining and imaging, transparent reporting, calibration, explainability, workflow integration and implementation economics. Future research should prioritize locally representative datasets, lightweight and edge-capable models, patient-level validation, human-in-the-loop decision support and implementation studies conducted within African pathology workflows.

title: Versajet® Hydrosurgery for Primary Axillary Hyperhidrosis with Osmidrosis: First Vietnamese Case Report with Histopathology
abstract: Abstract Background Conventional minimally invasive surgical techniques for axillary hyperhidrosis (e.g., cannula-assisted suction-curettage) carry risks of subdermal vascular plexus injury and flap necrosis (10–15%) [1] . The Versajet® Hydrosurgery System, employing the Venturi effect with high-pressure saline jet and continuous suction without thermal injury, represents a potential alternative [2,3] . Case presentation : A 33-year-old Vietnamese male (BMI 33.3 kg/m²) presented with 16-year history of bilateral primary axillary hyperhidrosis with osmidrosis (onset at age 18), HDSS 3 bilaterally, wet earwax phenotype (suggesting ABCC11 G-allele), DLQI 9/30, Park-Shin grade 3, meeting 5/6 Hornberger criteria [4] . Methods Surgery was performed on 23 April 2026 under Klein tumescent anesthesia (lidocaine 480 mg + epinephrine 1:1,000,000 + 500 mL 0.9% NaCl; 100 mL/axilla infiltration). The Versajet® II with a 45°/14 mm handpiece at power 6–8 (574 bar/8,330 psi) was used, consuming 500 mL 0.9% NaCl and 15 minutes of debridement per axilla through a 5-cm incision parallel to the axillary crease. Outcomes were assessed at 1 and 3 months using HDSS, DLQI, Park-Shin, and VSS, with paired pre-/post-excision histopathology. Results Total operative time was 100 minutes with blood loss < 30 mL and no intraoperative complications. VAS pain was 3/10 on days 1–3, resolving to 0/10 by day 10. At 3 months: HDSS 3→1, DLQI 9→1, Park-Shin 3→1, VSS 4/14, Clavien-Dindo grade I, patient satisfaction 5/5. Histopathology demonstrated 68.8–75.0% apocrine gland reduction and 32.3–45.5% eccrine gland reduction with preserved hair follicle architecture. Conclusion Hydrosurgery with the Versajet® System demonstrated high technical feasibility, significant clinical efficacy, and objective histopathological evidence of selective apocrine gland reduction while preserving the subdermal vascular plexus. Larger prospective cohort studies with long-term follow-up are warranted to standardize parameters and assess recurrence.

title: Associations of initial blood gas parameters with post-cooling MRI-derived brain volumes and Rutherford injury scores in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a retrospective exploratory study
abstract: Abstract Background Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may reveal structural alterations not captured by conventional visual assessment in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). This study investigated associations between initial blood gas parameters and post-cooling MRI-derived brain volumes and Rutherford MRI injury scores in neonates treated with therapeutic hypothermia. Methods This retrospective exploratory study included 79 neonates with HIE. Initial pH, partial pressure of carbon dioxide, bicarbonate, base excess, and lactate were evaluated in relation to 50 absolute MRI-derived brain-volume measures and the consensus Rutherford score. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlations and separate multivariable linear regression models adjusted for gestational age at birth, postnatal age at MRI, and sex, with HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. Two blinded radiologists independently assigned Rutherford scores and resolved disagreements by consensus. Secondary analyses compared neonates with pH ≤ 7.00 and pH > 7.00. The Benjamini–Hochberg procedure controlled the false discovery rate within prespecified analysis families. Results Consensus Rutherford scores were available for all 79 neonates (mean, 6.91 ± 1.34; median, 7; interquartile range, 6–8; range, 4–9). Interobserver agreement was good (absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.789; quadratic-weighted κ, 0.787); exact agreement occurred in 50.6% of examinations, and scores differed by no more than 1 point in 88.6%. After false-discovery-rate correction, no initial blood gas parameter was significantly associated with the consensus Rutherford score in either unadjusted or adjusted analyses. The adjusted mean score difference between the pH groups was−0.20 (95% confidence interval,−0.93 to 0.54; p = 0.597). No blood gas–volume association remained significant after correction, and no absolute or intracranial-volume-normalized measure differed significantly between the pH groups. Conclusions This exploratory cohort provided no evidence of associations between initial blood gas parameters and post-cooling Rutherford MRI injury scores or global and regional brain volumes after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings do not exclude clinically relevant associations and require confirmation in larger studies using neonatal-validated segmentation methods.

title: County-Level Radiologist Workforce Density, Cancer Mortality, and the Modeled Impact of AI-Augmented Diagnostic Capacity: A U.S. Ecological Analysis
abstract: Abstract Timely cancer diagnosis depends on adequate diagnostic imaging capacity, yet radiologist workforce availability remains unevenly distributed across U.S. counties. This study examined the association between county-level diagnostic radiologist density and age-adjusted cancer mortality across 3,073 U.S. counties using cross-sectional ecological analysis integrating provider enrollment, cancer registry, socioeconomic, and population data. In the fully adjusted model, higher log-transformed radiologist density was significantly associated with lower cancer mortality (β = −2.01 per 100,000; 95% CI: −2.82 to − 1.19; p < 0.001), with results robust to spatial autocorrelation (spatial error model β = −1.96) and twelve sensitivity analyses. Counties with zero radiologist presence (n = 1,334; population 22.6 million) were identified as having the greatest modeled mortality burden. Decision-analytic scenario modeling estimated that AI-equivalent augmentation matching the median nonzero-county density (ΔAI = 6.05 per 100,000) would correspond to a modeled annual mortality difference equivalent to approximately 887 deaths in this subgroup. The modeled association showed diminishing marginal differences, with larger estimated differentials when capacity was introduced into zero-radiologist counties than in higher-density settings. These findings suggest radiologist workforce distribution may represent a policy-relevant marker of diagnostic capacity and highlight zero-radiologist counties as targets for further evaluation of capacity-expanding interventions, including AI-equivalent approaches.

title: Habitat Radiomics-Based Stacking Ensemble Model for Predicting Disease-Free Survival in Early-Stage Cervical Cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose Despite undergoing curative surgery, about 30% of patients with early-stage cervical cancer (ECC) face the risk of recurrence. However, current prognostic tools are not very effective, with concordance index (C-index) typically ranging from 0.60 to 0.70. This study aimed to develop and validate a stacking survival ensemble model that incorporates intratumoral and peritumoral habitat radiomic features derived from routine preoperative multiparametric MRI to predict postoperative disease-free survival (DFS) in ECC. Methods This retrospective-prospective study enrolled 583 ECC patients (training: n = 293, internal validation: n = 165, external validation: n = 125). Habitat radiomic features were extracted from intratumoral and 3-mm peritumoral regions on preoperative T2WI, DWI, and CE-T1WI. A two-tier stacking survival ensemble framework was constructed with five base survival models (Cox regression, Random Survival Forest, Elastic Net-Cox, DeepSurv, and Support Vector Regression) and a Cox regression Meta-learner. Performance was assessed by C-index, time-dependent AUC, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. The incremental value of the model-derived lymph node metastasis probability (pLNM) from our prior classification model was also evaluated. Results The Meta-model achieved C-indices of 0.878, 0.868, and 0.848 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, outperforming most base models (P < 0.05). Externally, it yielded time-dependent AUCs of 0.887, 0.875, and 0.860 at 12, 24, and 36 months. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that the Meta-model effectively stratified into high- and low-risk groups with distinct DFS outcomes (log-rank P < 0.001 for all cohorts). Adding pLNM further improved C-index from 0.878 to 0.913 in the training cohort (P < 0.001). Conclusion The stacking survival ensemble model enables accurate postoperative risk stratification for ECC patients using routine preoperative MRI without additional imaging, potentially guiding individualized adjuvant therapy and surveillance intensity.

title: Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis Presenting with Spontaneous Pneumothorax and Osteolytic Lesions: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare myeloid neoplasm characterized by a highly heterogeneous clinical presentation, ranging from localized osseous lesions to multisystem disease involving high-risk organs. We report the case of a two-year-old girl who presented with persistent fever, dyspnea, and irritability. Initial chest radiography demonstrated a diffuse bilateral reticulonodular pulmonary pattern. During hospitalization, she developed a spontaneous right-sided pneumothorax associated with complete right lung atelectasis. Chest computed tomography revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary cystic lesions, while radiographs of the skull and long bones demonstrated multiple well-defined osteolytic lesions without periosteal reaction. The diagnosis of Langerhans cell histiocytosis was confirmed by histopathological examination. Despite intensive supportive management, the patient died seven days after admission because of severe pulmonary involvement. This case highlights the pivotal role of diagnostic imaging in the early recognition of multisystem LCH and underscores the importance of considering this entity in pediatric patients presenting with cystic lung disease accompanied by lytic bone lesions, as prompt diagnosis may facilitate appropriate management and improve clinical outcomes.

title: MCP-MedImg: Enabling Standardized PACS-AI Integration through the Model Context Protocol
abstract: Abstract Background: The proliferation of AI-assisted diagnostic models in medical imaging has created a fragmented integration landscape with PACS systems, leading to redundant development, inconsistent security compliance, and disconnected clinical workflows. Most AI diagnostic products exist as standalone Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), limiting scalability, auditability, and clinical adoption. Existing integration solutions (Direct Plugin, DICOM Router, VNA) are point-to-point adaptations without unified semantic layers. While the Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides tool invocation frameworks for AI agents, it lacks dedicated extensions for the medical imaging domain. Critically, global regulators (FDA, NMPA, EU) are converging on total product life cycle (TPLC) approaches demanding continuous post-market surveillance, yet no standardized protocol supports such surveillance at scale. Objective: We propose MCP-MedImg, an open reference architecture and protocol specification for interoperable integration and governance of AI services in medical imaging ecosystems, allowing AI capabilities to be discovered, invoked, monitored, and governed across heterogeneous healthcare environments without replacing existing PACS infrastructures. Methods: MCP-MedImg extends MCP with a four-layer architecture: Transport (DICOMweb-compatible, with dicom-mcp upward compatibility), Security and Compliance (PHI de-identification plus 14-column audit trail), AI Orchestration (model routing and version management), and Application Semantics (inspection-driven routing, lesion encoding, conditional human-in-the-loop verification). The specification defines six core information model entities and a tiered conformance model (five mandatory requirements, seven optional extensions). A reference implementation based on Orthanc PACS and nnU-Net validates protocol consistency, workflow, multi-model routing, DICOM SR/SEG generation, and audit trails. Results: The reference implementation demonstrated end-to-end interoperability, standardized service registration, structured result integration (DICOM SR/SEG), and auditable tracking of AI lifecycle events. On an NVIDIA RTX 4090 D, end-to-end latency under realistic clinical conditions was: LIDC-IDRI lung nodule CT (200 volumes, mean 5.4 s, P99 22.6 s) and MSD Heart cardiac MRI (10 volumes, mean 18.2 s, P99 27.6 s, 5-fold ensemble Dice 0.9324). Validation comprised 132 passing tests across 10 verification scenarios. Conclusions: MCP-MedImg aims to transform AI-assisted diagnosis from standalone software into auditable, service-oriented capabilities with conditional human-in-the-loop verification—directly addressing the regulatory surveillance gap and establishing foundations for governable public infrastructure in healthcare AI. By defining a tiered conformance model, the protocol enables incremental adoption: from minimal compliance (Level 1) through full production deployment (Level 3). The service-oriented delivery model, with built-in audit trails, configurable verification, and standardized output generation, significantly enhances clinical trust, lowers deployment barriers, and accelerates the adoption of AI-assisted diagnosis in routine clinical practice.

title: Bounded Repair Reachability of Residual Critical Blocks in 3D Binary Masks under SAFE-Gated Single-Voxel Flips
abstract: Abstract Critical configurations in three-dimensional binary images violate digital well-composedness, and voxel repairs can conflict with path constraints and foreground preservation. We formulate bounded repair reachability under single-voxel flips preserving the homotopy type of the foreground complex. We establish relations among admissible path sets and show that, under flip-once, endpoint and pathwise fidelity yield identical successful instances and shortest successful depths. Breadth-first search distinguishes found repairs, bounded absence and resource-limited outcomes. On 680 residual blocks from 222 Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2021 masks, unrestricted searches within radius 2 and depth 6 find repairs for 72 blocks under endpoint fidelity and 15 under pathwise fidelity. An endpoint-faithful witness temporarily removes and restores input foreground; a completed search excludes pathwise-faithful repair of that block within these bounds. These results distinguish the topological validity of moves from the admissibility of repair paths. Conclusions are limited to the stated windows, horizons and moves.

title: Central nervous system aspergillosis with negative serum fungal biomarkers after sequential teclistamab and talquetamab for multiple myeloma: a case report and review of the literature
abstract: Abstract Bispecific antibodies directed against B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) and G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D (GPRC5D) have improved outcomes in relapsed multiple myeloma but are associated with a high burden of infection. Invasive mould infection of the central nervous system (CNS) has rarely been described in this setting. We report a 70-year-old woman with heavily pretreated IgG-kappa myeloma who received teclistamab, complicated by immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) treated with corticosteroids, followed by talquetamab. She received antiviral and anti- Pneumocystis prophylaxis and intravenous immunoglobulin, without mould-active cover. Shortly after starting talquetamab, she developed cough and confusion, with cavitating pulmonary lesions initially attributed to bacterial abscesses. Serum galactomannan remained 0.1 on serial testing and β-D-glucan was negative. Computed tomography-guided lung biopsy confirmed pulmonary aspergillosis, and voriconazole was started. Failure to regain her functional baseline and progressive weakness, initially difficult to separate from her previous ICANS, led to brain magnetic resonance imaging, which showed a 10-mm ring-enhancing occipital lesion. Biopsy confirmed CNS aspergillosis. A literature review identified few published cases of invasive aspergillosis during bispecific therapy for myeloma, and serum galactomannan was positive in those with reported results. Negative fungal biomarkers should not exclude invasive aspergillosis in patients receiving bispecific antibodies, and new neurological decline warrants imaging and tissue diagnosis even after ICANS. Patients who require corticosteroids for ICANS during bispecific therapy, particularly after sequential bispecific exposure, may warrant individualised assessment of invasive mould risk and consideration of azole prophylaxis, pending prospective evaluation.

title: Functional and MRI improvement followed by a mixed trajectory during cannabinoid-terpenoid exposure in glioblastoma: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Glioblastoma has limited salvage options, while viable tumour, treatment injury, postoperative change, oedema and corticosteroid effects may produce overlapping clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings. Materials and Methods: Clinical records, serial MRI examinations and signed radiology reports were reviewed descriptively for a patient with IDH-wildtype, MGMT-promoter-methylated glioblastoma. The exposure history and contemporaneously documented neurological findings were aligned with seven MRI time points. No blinded central review, standardised volumetry or formal RANO 2.0 adjudication was performed. Results: After two operations, radiotherapy, concomitant temozolomide and three adjuvant cycles, serial MRI documented progression before April 2025. During a non-standard exposure state comprising intranasal perillyl alcohol and alpha-bisabolol, individualised cannabinoids and docosahexaenoic acid/medium-chain triglyceride oil, with dexamethasone fixed at 2 mg/day, hemiplegia/KPS 50 improved to hemiparesis with regained walking/KPS 80, coinciding with reduced enhancement. Later MRI showed increasing right temporal and cerebellar enhancement, including a new contralateral cerebellar focus, despite substantially stable postoperative cavity and T2/FLAIR extent. June 2026 lesion perfusion curves were low-amplitude without pathological hyperperfusion. The patient subsequently died after an overall survival of 45 months. Conclusions: This uncontrolled case documents early functional and radiological improvement on a stable corticosteroid background, followed by an anatomically progressive but biologically indeterminate trajectory. title: Neural correlates of empathy in autism: a coordinate-based meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose . Autistic and non-autistic people often differ in how readily they understand one another’s intentions and emotional states. Although empathy is commonly invoked to explain these differences, which components of empathic processing differ in autism, and their neural underpinnings, remain unclear. Methods . We conducted a pre-registered coordinate-based meta-analysis (activation likelihood estimation; ALE) of task-based fMRI studies of empathy in autism, examining within-group convergence, conjunction and between-group divergence separately for affective and cognitive components. Eleven studies (12 independent samples) met inclusion criteria, comprising 213 autistic and 216 non-autistic participants and 600 foci across 35 experiments; a multi-agent AI second reviewer supported screening and extraction. Results . Both groups shared a core empathy network (precuneus/posterior cingulate cortex, right middle temporal gyrus/posterior superior temporal sulcus, left inferior frontal gyrus, dorsomedial paracingulate), but the rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, a canonical cognitive-empathy hub, converged only in non-autistic participants. The between-group contrast was strongly asymmetric: non-autistic participants exceeded autistic convergence in ten regions, eight of them cognitive-empathy nodes, the largest in rostral dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; autistic participants exceeded non-autistic convergence in one region only, the posterior right temporoparietal junction. Subdomain analyses indicated relatively preserved convergence for affective empathy, with sparser, more diffuse overlap for cognitive empathy. Conclusion . These findings are consistent with a dissociation between relatively preserved affective and altered cognitive empathy in autism, and suggest a redistribution of activation within the mentalizing network rather than a global absence of empathy-related processing. Key words: autism spectrum disorder; empathy; activation likelihood estimation; functional magnetic resonance imaging; dorsomedial prefrontal cortex; temporoparietal junction

title: Exploring the Spectrum of Clinical and Radiological Findings in Active Tuberculosis
abstract: Abstract Background Clinical data may not accurately diagnose pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB), mainly due to manifestation overlap with other diseases, causing delays and misdiagnoses. Many gaps in the interpretation of clinical and radiographic findings were addressed and updated in our study. Methods An institutional-based study was carried out between 02/01/2018 and 26/06/2020 to clinically assess TB outpatients in high-burden zones. Those patients were identified through smear microscopy, GeneXpert Ultra, and chest X-rays and TB positives were interviewed. Of total, 329 patients were enrolled from Bench-Skeko, 23 from Skeka, and 29 from Keffa. Both descriptive and inferential statistics were performed using Stata 14/16. Results A total of 410 TB confirmed cases, with 328 (80%) being PTB, 79 (19.3%) EPTB, and 3 (0.73%) involving both forms were involved in this study. The mean age was 27.65 ± 11.44 years, with 55% male. Most patients were recently identified (99.3%). GeneXpert was used in 62.4%, AFB in 8.78%, and lesion biopsy or FNAC for EPTB in 16.83%, and 98% was on the intensive therapy for susceptible TB. A febrile episode was diagnosed in 93% (5.4% >40°C, 87% <39°C), night sweat in 93.17%, appetite loss in 89%, fatigue in 90%, and weight loss in 88%. Respiratory symptoms were very common, with cough reported in 94.2%: productive in 91%, and prolonged (> 3 wks) in 77%. Abnormalities in chest X ray were reported in 16.3%, with pleural effusion in 11.2%, cavitary formations in 13%, and lymph node enlarged in 14%. Blood pressure abnormalities were relatively low, with 76.3% having normal. Only few findings were reported as statistically significant predictors of active PTB. Chest abnormalities (OR = 6.87), prolonged cough (OR = 6.4), mucoid (OR = 14.6), and mucopurulent sputum (OR = 56.4) increased PTB odds, while lymphadenopathy was less commonly reported (OR = 0.16). Appetite loss (OR = 3.26), pleural effusion (OR = 2.41), and fibrosis (OR = 2.31) showed weak associations. Conclusions A high prevalence of the TB tetrad: prolonged cough, night sweat, fever and appetite loss were observed. PTB odds were higher with chest abnormalities, effusion, fibrosis, infiltration, and expansion, highlighting the diagnostic value of radiology. Clinical Trial Registration : No applicable

title: Unsupervised multimodal brain MRI registration with complementary learned and structural descriptors.
abstract: Abstract Deformable registration of T1- and T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance images is difficult because tissue intensities differ across contrasts. We investigate whether learned and hand-crafted descriptors provide complementary similarity information for unsupervised registration. A Cross-Modal Descriptor Network learns contrast-invariant voxel embeddings through self-supervised contrastive training on aligned same-subject pairs. These embeddings are combined with the modality-independent neighbourhood descriptor with self-similarity context (MIND-SSC) to train a compact diffeomorphic attention U-Net without anatomical labels. In inter-subject T1-to-T2 registration on the IXI dataset (n=45), the hybrid achieved a mean Dice coefficient of 0.700 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance of 3.21 mm, with no observed folded voxels. It outperformed the evaluated classical, learned, structural-descriptor, transformer, and foundation-model baselines (p<0.05, paired Wilcoxon tests). Gains were largest for small deep gray-matter structures, and the hybrid also performed best in the evaluated unseen-scanner and BraTS glioma experiments. Descriptors are used only during training; inference requires one 83 ms forward pass of a 0.247 M-parameter network. These results support combining learned and structural descriptors for accurate and computationally efficient multimodal brain registration.

title: Enhanced Breast Cancer Classification by Integrating CNN and ViT on the CBIS-DDSM Mammography Dataset
abstract: Abstract Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality among women worldwide, necessitating early and accurate diagnostic methods to improve patient outcomes. This study presents a novel hybrid approach for breast cancer classification by integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures, specifically applied to the publicly available CBIS-DDSM mammography dataset. The initial phase employs a CNN model, which excels in localized feature extraction through convolutional layers, to identify key patterns related to benign and malignant tumors. However, CNNs inherently focus on local features and may overlook broader contextual relationships within the image. To overcome this limitation, the study introduces a hybrid framework that combines CNN with the Vision Transformer model. ViT utilizes self-attention mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies and global context, complementing the localized feature extraction capability of CNNs. By integrating these two deep learning paradigms, the hybrid model effectively captures both fine-grained local details and overarching structural patterns within mammograms. Experimental results indicate that synergy results in an improved classification accuracy. The enhanced performance of the combined CNN-ViT model underscores the potential of hybrid deep learning strategies in medical image analysis. Moreover, this approach demonstrates robust generalization on the CBIS-DDSM dataset, which includes diverse mammographic cases. The findings not only provide a pathway to more reliable breast cancer detection tools but also contribute to reducing diagnostic burden and improving early intervention strategies.

title: Intelligent System for Celiac Disease Detection Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Abstract In this study authors explore the application of deep learning techniques for the early detection of celiac disease through the analysis of medical imaging and clinical data. We used the convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed model exhibits promising accuracy in identifying patterns indicative of celiac disease from diverse images of a big database. The integration of deep learning in celiac disease diagnosis holds the potential for enhancing early intervention and improving patient outcomes, marking a significant advancement in medical diagnostics. The proposed approach elucidates the intricacies of celiac disease and implements a robust Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for accurate image classification. Achieving an average accuracy of 96%, this method promises enhanced diagnosis and management, paving the way for personalized healthcare interventions with significant improvements in patient outcomes and quality of life.

title: Multi-Task Framework for Efficient Knee Osteoarthritis Segmentation and Classification
abstract: Abstract Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a leading cause of chronic disability worldwide, and magnetic reso- nance imaging (MRI) remains the gold standard for assessing cartilage and meniscal integrity. While 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can leverage volumetric context for KOA analysis, they often incur high computational cost, increased memory demands, and susceptibility to learning from anatomically irrelevant regions. In this work, we propose a unified and flexible multi-task learning framework that accommodates both 2D slice-based and 3D volume-based convolutional backbones for joint KOA classification and knee structure segmentation. The architecture integrates a shared encoder configurable as either 2D or 3D followed by two task-specific branches: a dual-headed segmentation decoder for meniscus and cartilage masks, and a classification head operating on globally pooled features for KOA detection. We train and validate the framework on a large-scale dataset of 105,919 MRI slices, including expert-annotated segmentation masks and radiographically verified KOA labels. The multi-task design enables concurrent learning of anatomical and diagnostic signals at either the slice or volume level, improving task synergy and anatomical focus. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that the 2D variant achieves more consistent segmentation quality, faster convergence, and lower computational overhead than a 3D VGG-UNet baseline while also delivering improved KOA classification accuracy.

title: Joint Classification and Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning for Cervical Cancer Detection in Histopathological Images
abstract: Abstract Correct categorization of histopathological images of the cervix is very crucial if one is to identify and treat any emerging cases of cervical cancer on time. However, this is not an easy task, given that there is so much variability within one class while there are only minute distinctions between normal and pathological tissues. In our study, we therefore develop a deep learning approach that combines contrast learning with the traditional approach of using the cross-entropy loss function to correctly categorize histopathological images of the cervix into normal or pathological tissues. Our approach is based on ResNet-50 and seeks to maximize both learning of appropriate features and correct classification of images into one of two classes: normal or pathological cervical tissues. Performance is evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation on a variety of metrics, including balanced accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, as well as average precision. For the histopathological dataset, CAISHI, this approach in all cases produces very high balanced accuracy of 96.90 ± 0.23 on average. High precision, recall, and F1 values indicate a high accuracy of abnormal region detection. In comparison to existing machine learning techniques, CNN models, transformer networks, and a few-shot learning strategy, the proposed approach demonstrates improved robustness and generalization capabilities. From the results, it can be inferred that the integration of supervised contrastive learning with deep convolutional feature extraction leads to a dramatic improvement in the representation ability and classification accuracy in the field of cervical histopathology images. The proposed framework can indeed be used as a robust interpretation solution with high potential for medical support in cervical cancer diagnosis.

title: QSGT: Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer for Faithful Multi-modal Radiology Report Summarization
abstract: Abstract Improving the alignment between visual evidence andtextual descriptions in medical vision-language models(VLM) remains a critical challenge for achieving entitylevelfaithfulness in low-resource generation tasks. Thispaper proposes Quantum-Inspired Sparse Gated Transformer(QSGT), a hybrid approach of token pruningand mixture of experts (MoE), grounded on the conceptionof quantum many-body wavefunction. This hybridapproach was aimed at improving the selectionof both modality-specific expert tokens and the formationof non-dominating experts to determine stableconjugates. The token pruning approach was improvedusing the quantum orbital style token assignments andthe mixture of experts by the quantum doubly occupancyapproximation. We also introduce two clinicallymotivated regularization terms, pair loss and seniorityloss, further enforce semantic consistency and dominanceof diagnostically relevant features. Our extensiveexperiments across seven thoracic disease categoriesdemonstrate that QSGT significantly outperforms stateof-the-art medical VLMs on multiple evaluation metrics,including RadGraph (36.2), SPICE (42.68), andconsistently high BERTScore (98), on the MIMIC-CXRtest set. QSGT achieves substantial gains in clinical correctnessand semantic accuracy, particularly for complexconditions such as pneumonia and pneumothorax. Ablationstudies confirmthe importance of each architecturalcomponent, while convergence analyses show stable andinterpretable learning dynamics. These results indicate that QSGT provides a robust and clinically meaningfulsolution for multimodal medical report summarization,enabling more reliable, interpretable, and patientcentredclinical AI systems.

title: Resistance to thyroid hormone β (RTHβ) due to a THRB mutation (p.Arg429Gln) in a39-year-old woman initially treated for thyrotoxicosis
abstract: Abstract Background Resistance to thyroid hormone beta (RTHβ) is a rare inherited disorder characterised by elevated free thyroid hormone levels with non-suppressed or elevated TSH, most commonly caused by mutations in the THRB gene. The biochemical profile often mimics thyrotoxicosis or a TSH secreting pituitary adenoma, contributing to delayed or inappropriate treatment. Methods We describe the clinical course, biochemical findings and genetic analysis of a 39 year old woman who presented with palpitations, hypertension and elevated FT4 and FT3 despite a non-suppressed TSH, and who demonstrated no response to antithyroid medication. Genetic sequencing was performed. Results Initial testing showed normal TSH levels (2.45 mU/L), and elevated FT4 (29 pmol/L) and FT3 (7.6 pmol/L). Antithyroid therapy (Thiamazole) led to a paradoxal rise in TSH. Pituitary MRI was normal. Genetic analysis identified a heterozygous THRB gene variant, NM_001354712.2:c.1286G>A (p.Arg429Gln), classified as pathogenic. Antithyroid therapy was discontinued, and management was transitioned to betablockade. The patient remained clinically stable at a 24-months follow-up, and genetic counselling was initiated. Conclusion This case highlights that elevated FT4/FT3 with inappropriately normal or high TSH should raise suspicion of RTHβ. Genetic confirmation is critical to avoid unnecessary interventions and to guide appropriate long-term management and family screening.

title: Deep learning-assisted target volume segmentation for uterine malignancies on non-contrast CT
abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate delineation of clinical target volume (CTV) and planning target volume (PTV) is essential for radiotherapy in uterine malignancies. However, the limited soft-tissue contrast of non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) makes automated target segmentation challenging. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 157 unique patients. Of these, 137 patients were used for model development and internal testing, including a development cohort of 110 patients and an independent test cohort of 27 patients. A separate cohort of 20 patients was used for workflow evaluation. A multi-label nnU-Net model was developed to simultaneously segment the CTV and PTV. Four nnU-Net configurations were compared using five-fold cross-validation. Segmentation performance was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and the 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95). Three radiation oncologists independently assessed the clinical acceptability of the auto-contours using a four-point Likert scale. Workflow efficiency was evaluated by comparing manual contouring with AI-assisted contour editing. Results: The 3D-fullres configuration achieved the numerically highest overall cross-validation performance and was selected for independent internal testing. In the 27-patient independent test cohort, the mean DSC was 90.02% ± 2.33% for PTV and 72.16% ± 4.54% for CTV. The corresponding median HD95 values were 5.12 mm (interquartile range [IQR], 5.00–7.60 mm) and 5.55 mm (IQR, 5.00–9.50 mm), respectively. Rating-level clinical acceptability was 91.4% for PTV and 75.3% for CTV. Inter-rater agreement was higher for PTV than for CTV. In the separate workflow cohort, AI-assisted contouring reduced the mean total task time from 65.4 to 14.2 minutes per case, corresponding to an observed reduction of 78.3% (P<0.001). Conclusion: The multi-label 3D-fullres nnU-Net achieved high PTV overlap and moderate CTV overlap on internal NCCT data and reduced contouring time in a separate workflow cohort. The model may provide editable initial contours, but CTV predictions require careful physician review. External validation and dosimetric assessment are required before routine clinical use.

Results: The 3D-fullres configuration achieved the numerically highest overall cross-validation performance and was selected for independent internal testing. In the 27-patient independent test cohort, the mean DSC was 90.02% ± 2.33% for PTV and 72.16% ± 4.54% for CTV. The corresponding median HD95 values were 5.12 mm (interquartile range [IQR], 5.00–7.60 mm) and 5.55 mm (IQR, 5.00–9.50 mm), respectively. Rating-level clinical acceptability was 91.4% for PTV and 75.3% for CTV. Inter-rater agreement was higher for PTV than for CTV. In the separate workflow cohort, AI-assisted contouring reduced the mean total task time from 65.4 to 14.2 minutes per case, corresponding to an observed reduction of 78.3% (P<0.001). Conclusion: The multi-label 3D-fullres nnU-Net achieved high PTV overlap and moderate CTV overlap on internal NCCT data and reduced contouring time in a separate workflow cohort. The model may provide editable initial contours, but CTV predictions require careful physician review. External validation and dosimetric assessment are required before routine clinical use.

title: Energy-Based Devices for GLP-1 Receptor Agonist-Associated Facial Aging: A Tissue-Specific Safety Framework.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA)-associated rapid weight loss may be accompanied by facial changes resembling accelerated aging, colloquially termed "Ozempic face". In this review, this proposed phenotype is termed GLP-1RA-associated facial accelerated aging (GLP-1RA-FAA) and is characterized primarily by facial volume loss and skin laxity, with possible but incompletely characterized alterations in dermal-adipose support, adipose-derived stem-cell biology, fibroblast-extracellular-matrix homeostasis, and facial muscle. Demand for energy-based device (EBD) treatment in this population is increasing; however, whether conventional EBD parameters are effective or safe in medication-associated facial volume depletion is unknown. A narrative review was informed by structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 through August 31, 2026. Evidence was selected for clinical directness and relevance to radiofrequency, high-intensity focused ultrasound, broadband light, microwave, extracorporeal shock wave therapy, diode laser, and synchronized radiofrequency with high-intensity facial electrical stimulation. Available modalities differ in their intended tissue depth and in the potential relevance of three conceptual targets: preservation of adipose tissue, dermal fibroblast-extracellular-matrix remodeling, and facial muscle-SMAS support. Preclinical body-contouring studies suggest that sustained subcutaneous heating in the approximate 43-45°C range can be associated with adipocyte injury or apoptosis; however, no facial thermal dose threshold has been established, particularly in GLP-1RA-treated patients. No individual EBD modality has demonstrated simultaneous restoration of adipose, dermal, and muscle-related targets in prospective GLP-1RA-specific studies. Conservative control of treatment depth, careful avoidance of unnecessary deep energy deposition in volume-depleted regions, investigation of low-intensity dermal remodeling strategies, and evaluation of muscle-targeting approaches are proposed as research considerations. These concepts are hypothesis generating and do not constitute clinical recommendations or standards of care. Prospective controlled studies in well-characterized GLP-1RA-treated populations are required before device-specific protocols can be adopted.

title: Localized Bullous Pemphigoid of the Scalp and Face with Suspected Vulvar Involvement: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Localized bullous pemphigoid (LBP) is a form of bullous pemphigoid (BP) confined to a limited anatomical area. Classification becomes less certain when clinically similar lesions occur at a distant site without site-specific immunopathologic confirmation. We report immunopathologically supported scalp/facial BP-spectrum disease with a temporally associated but unconfirmed vulvar eruption. Case presentation A 51-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of pruritic erythema and tense bullae on the scalp and face and a 1-month history of erythematous scaly plaques with hemorrhagic bullous lesions in the vulvar region. Scalp histopathology showed a subepidermal blister with eosinophil-rich inflammation, and direct immunofluorescence (DIF) of perilesional scalp skin showed linear IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane zone. Infectious studies of the vulvar eruption were negative. Anti-BP180/230 serology, indirect immunofluorescence, salt-split skin studies, and anti-type VII collagen antibody testing were unavailable. Vulvar biopsy and DIF were not performed; therefore, vulvar BP could not be confirmed. With systemic and topical corticosteroids plus adjunctive minocycline, no new bullae developed by day 5, and the lesions markedly improved within 2 weeks. Methylprednisolone was subsequently tapered from 40 mg/day to a maintenance dose of 4 mg/day; minocycline and topical corticosteroids were discontinued after sustained clinical improvement. At 6 months, the disease remained clinically controlled on methylprednisolone 4 mg/day, with no new bullae or clinically evident recurrence. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Conclusion The findings support localized BP/BP-spectrum disease of the scalp and face, while the vulvar eruption remains unconfirmed. The parallel treatment response is supportive but not diagnostic of vulvar BP. When feasible, lesions at sensitive sites should undergo site-specific biopsy and DIF. If biopsy is declined or impractical, pretreatment morphology should be carefully documented, diagnostic uncertainty should be acknowledged, and follow-up should assess for scarring and additional mucosal involvement.

title: Scleroderma-Like Skin Changes and Multifocal Muscle Thickening in a Patient with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Paraneoplastic rheumatic manifestations may precede the diagnosis of an occult malignancy and closely mimic primary autoimmune connective-tissue diseases. Scleroderma-like manifestations have rarely been reported in association with lymphoid malignancies, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Case presentation A 47-year-old woman presented with progressive skin thickening, difficulty walking, reduced appetite, and weight loss. She had been diagnosed with scleroderma by an outside physician in early 2024 and had been treated with methotrexate 15 mg once weekly. Physical examination revealed facial skin tightening, sclerodactyly, skin induration extending to the wrists and elbows, and asymmetric thickening of the right neck, forearm, and thigh muscles. Pruritic migratory annular plaques were observed on the trunk and resolved spontaneously within two weeks, clinically suggesting an erythema annulare centrifugum-like eruption. Raynaud phenomenon was absent, antinuclear antibody testing was negative, and cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy was present. Computed tomography demonstrated multiple destructive osteolytic lesions in the lumbar vertebrae. Neck magnetic resonance imaging showed edema-like T2 hyperintensity involving the sternocleidomastoid muscle and adjacent tissues without contrast enhancement. Biopsy of a vertebral lesion revealed DLBCL, with tumor cells positive for leukocyte common antigen and CD20 and a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 80%. The patient was started on standard first-line R-CHOP immunochemotherapy but died in the intensive care unit after the first treatment administration, precluding assessment of treatment response and longer-term follow-up. Conclusion This case illustrates an unusual presentation of DLBCL accompanied by scleroderma-like cutaneous changes, multifocal muscle thickening, and an annular eruption. The simultaneous absence of Raynaud phenomenon and antinuclear antibodies, together with constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy, asymmetric soft-tissue abnormalities, and destructive bone lesions, should prompt reconsideration of presumed systemic sclerosis and evaluation for an underlying malignancy. Although a paraneoplastic association was strongly suspected, it could not be confirmed because the patient died after the first treatment administration, precluding assessment of the rheumatic manifestations after lymphoma-directed therapy.
